items.title: bk9cj/manus--ai
items.description: AI Manus is a general-purpose AI Agent system that supports running various tools and operations in a sandbox environment.
items.ai_summary: Autonomous AI agent system designed to run code and control a web browser in a sandbox environment for task automation.

items.title: ATLURI0001/NeuroMirror
items.description: Real-time webcam-driven anatomical visualization with interactive X-ray simulations of cranial, neural, and muscular structures.
items.ai_summary: Web-based augmented reality application that uses a standard webcam for real-time anatomical and neural X-ray visualization of cranial and muscular structures.

items.title: The Noise Floor of a Quantization Comparison: Engine, restart, batch and kernel drift, measured against 8-bit and 4-bit effects in two decision models
items.description: A quantized model is usually judged by comparing it with its BF16 original, but that comparison changes more than the weights.

items.title: BitDecoding-FP4: Native FP4 KV Cache Decoding via Algorithm-System Co-Design
items.description: BitDecoding-FP4 co-designs FP4 quantization and system optimizations to enable accurate, high-throughput long-context KV decoding for LLMs.

items.title: HuggingFaceTB/SmolVLM2-256M-Video-Instruct
items.description: Vision-language model from HuggingFaceTB. 43.6k downloads and 208 likes so far.

items.title: Google's AI answers reducing search traffic by 40%
items.description: Trending on Hacker News from revscope.co. 305 points and 240 comments.
items.ai_summary: Google's AI answers reduce clicks to outside websites by about 40 percent while appearing on more than half of tracked US keywords.

items.title: Managed NVIDIA Dynamo on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod Inference
items.description: Amazon SageMaker HyperPod Inference now supports NVIDIA Dynamo for distributed inference, with multi-node and disaggregated serving, KV-aware routing, and automatic fault recovery. Serve large models across many nodes without building the orchestration layer yourself.
items.ai_summary: Amazon SageMaker HyperPod Inference now supports managed NVIDIA Dynamo for distributed inference, enabling multi-node serving with automatic fault recovery.

items.title: External sandboxes for coding agents
items.description: External sandboxes for coding agents I've been exploring new ways to sandbox code that is executed by agents, with a focus on making it safer to try out local models without worrying that a mistake or prompt injection attack might cause them to take damaging actions on a…
items.ai_summary: External sandboxes for coding agents provide a safer way to execute local code and protect against prompt injection attacks or mistakes.

items.title: Reducing token costs and latency in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore JSON workloads
items.description: As production agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore process multi-megabyte JSON payloads, token costs and latency climb. This post shares three composable strategies: offloading heavy artifacts to Amazon S3, on-demand result paging, and dictionary compaction.
items.ai_summary: Three composable strategies for Amazon Bedrock AgentCore reduce token costs and latency when processing multi-megabyte JSON payloads in production agents.

items.title: GPT‑6.2 Astra and GPT‑6.2 Sol
items.description: GPT‑6.2 Astra and GPT‑6.2 Sol OpenAI: We’re introducing GPT‑6.2 Astra, our new frontier model for your hardest projects, and GPT‑6.2 Sol, our efficient, versatile model for everyday work. They're available in the API as gpt-6.2-astra and gpt-6.2-sol .
items.ai_summary: OpenAI introduces GPT-6.2 Astra for hard projects and GPT-6.2 Sol as an efficient, versatile model for everyday work.

items.title: Harvard researchers find AI coding agents shifted the bottleneck to code review
items.description: Trending on Hacker News from complexdiscovery.com. 157 points and 200 comments.
items.ai_summary: A Harvard study reveals that AI coding agents increased code output by 30 percent while making code reviews take 49 percent longer.

items.title: Cut generative AI costs: Code for rules, models for judgment
items.description: The biggest cost lever in a generative AI system is whether you call a model at all. Learn how to decide whether each workflow step needs a model, and map each option to AWS: deterministic code, a constrained decision call, or a right-sized model on Amazon Bedrock.
items.ai_summary: A guide for generative AI workloads helps determine when to use deterministic code, constrained decisions, or right-sized models to reduce costs.

items.title: Amazon SageMaker AI real-time endpoints now support KV cache aware routing
items.description: Amazon SageMaker AI real-time endpoints now support KV cache-aware routing, a new strategy that routes each request to the instance holding the longest cached match for its prompt.
items.ai_summary: Amazon SageMaker AI real-time endpoints now support KV cache-aware routing to direct prompts to instances holding the longest cached match.

items.title: Ambient LLMs: Data-Efficient Supervised Fine-tuning via Temperature Matching
items.description: Collecting large-scale, diverse, and high-quality post-training datasets for autoregressive language models is challenging.
items.ai_summary: Ambient SFT matches high-temperature distributions with a pre-trained teacher model, improving domain adaptation and instruction-tuning while preventing overfitting.

items.title: Spool: Low-Latency Streaming Inference for Hybrid Vision-Language Models
items.description: Applications such as visual accessibility agents and robotics require answering questions about recent video content promptly, over a bounded window of past frames (e.g., the last two minutes).
items.ai_summary: Spool is a training-free framework that caches per-frame state transformations to achieve low-latency streaming inference in hybrid vision-language models.

items.title: FastFrames: Video Generation at Interactive Latency
items.description: Autoregressive video diffusion models generate frames based on new observations and inputs, making them a promising medium for interactive visual experiences. However, existing models are orders of magnitude too slow for fluid interaction.

items.title: StringQFT: A Multiuse Textbook Resource for AI-Assisted Theoretical Physics
items.description: We present StringQFT as a textbook collection for string constructions of quantum field theory and as infrastructure for AI-assisted theoretical physics.
items.ai_summary: StringQFT is an 18-volume textbook collection and infrastructure resource designed to support AI-assisted theoretical physics research and agents.

items.title: An inexact stochastic variance-reduced gradient method for constrained convex finite-sum optimization
items.description: In this paper, we study a class of constrained convex finite-sum optimization problems. In many practical applications, all or some of the constraints are hard constraints that represent imperative requirements.
items.ai_summary: An inexact stochastic variance-reduced gradient method improves first-order oracle complexity for solving constrained convex finite-sum optimization problems.

items.title: Do LLM Agents Still Need to Be Told How to Self-Improve?
items.description: Capable frozen LLM agents can autonomously construct context-based self-learning algorithms from basic resources and a general goal, yielding text artifacts that transfer to new game and 3D navigation tasks.

items.title: What Does a Bias Head Measure? Non-Identifiability in Head-Level Bias Attribution
items.description: Methods that localise social bias in large language models to individual attention heads and remove it by ablation are validated by their effect on a fairness metric, never by evidence that the statistic selecting the heads measures bias.
items.ai_summary: An audit of social bias attribution methods in large language models finds that head-level bias metrics are non-identifiable and fail to reduce unfairness.

items.title: Higher-Scoring Coding Models Did Not Get More Work Done
items.description: New coding models advertise themselves on score improvements of coding benchmarks. Yet no study has tested if a model that scores higher on these benchmarks gets more real work done. On June 12, 2026, a U.S.
items.ai_summary: Empirical analysis of 297 users finds that switching to higher-scoring coding models does not significantly increase real-world software engineering productivity or pull request merge rates.

items.title: EviSlide-MIL: Multi-Query Pooling and Shared Prediction for Class-Incremental Whole-Slide Image Classification
items.description: Histopathological analysis of whole-slide images (WSIs) plays a critical role in cancer diagnosis, and multiple instance learning (MIL) is widely adopted for WSI analysis under weak supervision.
items.ai_summary: EviSlide-MIL is a class-incremental whole-slide image classification framework that uses multi-query pooling and a shared prediction module to learn new tumor subtypes while preventing catastrophic forgetting.

items.title: Multimodal Masked Diffusion Autoencoder for Modeling Impaired Driving
items.description: Human cognitive state (e.g., distraction, stress), gaze, and behavior interact with the driving environment in subtle ways that AI could use to assist drivers, but ground-truth labels for human cognitive state levels are costly to obtain at scale.
items.ai_summary: ID-MAE is a multimodal masked-diffusion autoencoder that improves driver impairment prediction by jointly reconstructing gaze, trajectory, and impairment tokens from driving-simulator data.

items.title: Learning Grounded Reasoning from Human Gaze
items.description: Human visual reasoning is driven by systematic exploration and extraction of task-relevant visual evidence. Human gaze provides a window into this process, making gaze a useful source of guidance for visually-grounded reasoning in vision-language models (VLMs).
items.ai_summary: GGR is a vision-language reasoning model that uses human gaze data as a spatial exploration prior to improve visual grounding and task accuracy across chart understanding and counting tasks.

items.title: Distortion-Free Semantic Watermarks for Black-Box Generative Models
items.description: We present a provably distortion-free semantic watermarking algorithm that requires only black-box sampling access to a generative model and black-box access to a semantic embedding.
items.ai_summary: Semantic watermarking algorithm provides provably distortion-free watermarks for black-box generative models that remain robust to content-preserving image transformations like compression and cropping.

items.title: Reading Scene States: Uncovering Safety Failures in Vision-Language Models
items.description: Vision-language models (VLMs) can provide harmful assistance by interpreting visual events, even without an explicit request for the underlying harmful objective.
items.ai_summary: SceneSafetyBench and the S3TA attack framework reveal a security vulnerability where vision-language models generate harmful assistance when prompted with scene-state descriptions instead of direct requests.

items.title: Fine-Tuning Gemma 4 Edge Models for MATLAB Signal-Processing Code with SFT and QLoRA on a Laptop iGPU
items.description: Small language models that run on a laptop are attractive for writing signal-processing code offline, but they make systematic errors on digital signal processing (DSP) conventions.
items.ai_summary: Supervised fine-tuning using LoRA and QLoRA on a laptop integrated GPU adapts Gemma 4 edge models to correctly generate digital signal processing code in MATLAB.

items.title: Agent Trust Infrastructure (ATI): A Federated Identity, Trust, Attestation, and Accountability Architecture for Cross-Organization Autonomous AI Agents
items.description: AI agents increasingly collaborate across organizational boundaries, invoking tools and interacting with agents operated by independent entities.
items.ai_summary: Agent Trust Infrastructure is a framework-independent security architecture using public key infrastructure and remote attestation to verify cross-organizational identity and authorization for collaborative AI agents.

items.title: Learned versus Kinematic Trajectory Prediction under Reduced Observation Frequency
items.description: Trajectory prediction models for automated driving are usually trained on data with a fixed sampling frequency, while positions received via vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication arrive at 1-10 Hz.
items.ai_summary: Evaluation of trajectory prediction models shows that learned recurrent neural networks maintain their accuracy advantage over kinematic models even when observation history frequencies drop down to 1 Hz.

items.title: Structure--Residual Inductive Biases for Language Model Pretraining
items.description: Next-token prediction is relied upon to learn both predictive behavior and internal representations. We ask whether representation structure itself should be an explicit inductive bias.
items.ai_summary: Structure-residual inductive biases combining boundary bottlenecks and continuous geometry regularization improve language model pretraining efficiency by separating global structure from local realization details.

items.title: WoRD: Diffusion-Based Posterior Inference for Online Goal Recognition
items.description: Goal recognition is the task of inferring an agent's intended goal from its observed behavior. Most existing work focuses on high-level symbolic recognition, abstracting away the continuous motion through which agents reach their goal.
items.ai_summary: Waypoint Recognition with Diffusion is a diffusion-based inference method that infers an agent's intended goal from partial observations by running denoising chains per candidate goal.

items.title: Retrieval-Augmented Correction for Generalist Medical Image Segmentation
items.description: Automated segmentation is routinely used as the first step in quantitative image-based clinical workflows, where predicted masks are subsequently reviewed and corrected by human operators.
items.ai_summary: GRACE is a retrieval-augmented medical image segmentation refiner that edits input masks using context from a shared knowledge base of verified prior cases.

items.title: Any2Building: Unifying Point Clouds and Images for Building Reconstruction via Shared Spatial Queries
items.description: Abstracting structured buildings from limited observations is essential for 3D urban modeling and digital twins.
items.ai_summary: Any2Building is a unified framework utilizing shared spatial queries to reconstruct Level of Detail 2 building models from partial point clouds, overhead images, or both.

items.title: Polarity Composition Hypothesis: Causal Evidence from Negation in NLI
items.description: We investigate how language models process negation in natural language inference (NLI). We propose the \textit{Polarity Composition Hypothesis}, a high-level causal model of this computation.
items.ai_summary: The polarity composition hypothesis is a causal model for how language models process negation in natural language inference, supported by identified causally effective subspaces.

items.title: Fold Weighting for Cross-Validation Under Continuous Distributional Drift
items.description: Cross-validation weights all folds equally, so under drift the oldest folds count as much as the newest.
items.ai_summary: Sliding-window cross-validation with advance-fixed fold weights minimizes a convex bound on deployment risk under continuous distributional drift by shifting weight toward recent data.

items.title: Say Less, Hallucinate Less? Diagnosing and Restoring Object Coverage in Preference-Optimized Vision-Language Models
items.description: Preference optimization (PO) is the standard way to reduce object hallucination in large vision-language models. We find that four public PO checkpoints of LLaVA-1.5-7B also lower object coverage.
items.ai_summary: Base-guided object-category restoration appends high-confidence base-only object categories to preference-optimized vision-language model captions without training to recover lost recall.

items.title: Déjà View: A Shared Working-Memory Model for Visual Tasks
items.description: A working-memory model must remember stimuli and use its memory flexibly to perform different tasks. Here we introduce a model of working memory for images that combines dynamic activity with temporary associations between image features.
items.ai_summary: A working-memory model combining dynamic activity with temporary feature associations performs multiple visual tasks and demonstrates how errors depend on task demands and image history.

items.title: Inference after coding agents
items.description: Empirical research is changing rapidly as AI coding agents are becoming increasingly proficient in every step of it, from writing code to manipulating data.
items.ai_summary: A correction procedure for AI coding agent analyses uses data subsampling and agent replay to detect and correct distortions caused by selective inference during empirical research.

items.title: Not Everything Needs an LLM
items.description: Trending on Hacker News from newsletter.posthog.com. 144 points and 59 comments.
items.ai_summary: Decision models provide fast, structured, and probabilistic answers for simpler tasks as a cost-effective alternative to large language models.

items.title: Attribution Through the Decoder: Prediction-Space Explanations for Structured Outputs
items.description: Networks that predict angles, gaze directions, and rotations do not output these quantities directly: they emit raw coordinates that a fixed decoder, such as normalization, maps to the final prediction.
items.ai_summary: Tangent attribution methods account for fixed decoders when explaining structured outputs like angles and rotations, improving explanation accuracy by avoiding irrelevant raw coordinate attributions.

items.title: MoE--LoRA Methods for Multilingual Adaptation: A Systematic Empirical Study
items.description: Routed low-rank adapters offer a parameter-efficient means to improve the performance of large language models (LLMs) across tasks.
items.ai_summary: An empirical study evaluating eight low-rank adaptation methods across 200 languages demonstrates that these methods improve translation fit and benefit low-resource languages most.

items.title: TextSphere: Efficient Text-to-Image Generation via Shared Hyperspherical Alignment and Uniformity
items.description: Recent advances in text-to-image generation have substantially improved image quality, particularly through diffusion-based methods that require multiple inference steps.
items.ai_summary: TextSphere is an efficient text-to-image generative framework that extends Sphere Encoder with language conditioning and cross-modal alignment to improve generation quality while using fewer sampling steps.

items.title: Learning Stratified Policies for Inference-Time Objectives
items.description: Inference-time scaling improves the performance of large language models by sampling multiple responses and evaluating their collective utility. However, many existing approaches obtain these samples by repeatedly sampling from a single policy.
items.ai_summary: Stratified policies allocate the inference-time sample budget across a population of learned LoRA adapters on a shared language model backbone, improving pass@k performance on reasoning tasks.

items.title: VIVID: Beyond Static Multi-Image Reasoning with Localized Visual Differences and Textual Entity Dynamics in Video MLLMs
items.description: Video question answering under tight frame budgets requires preserving localized motion and event order, yet current video multimodal large language models (MLLMs) reduce comprehension to static multi-image reasoning by discarding unselected frames and encoding keyframes…
items.ai_summary: VIVID is a video multimodal large language model that uses keyframes and inter-frame patch differences to preserve localized motion and event order for efficient video question answering.

items.title: Capability Composition in Heterogeneous Teams via Barrier-Guided Diffusion Sampling
items.description: The agents in a heterogeneous team can cooperate to accomplish tasks that exceed their individual capabilities.
items.ai_summary: Capability Composition via Barrier-Guided Diffusion Sampling is a method that enforces physical trajectory constraints to generate cooperative behaviors in heterogeneous robot teams without needing demonstration data.

items.title: $π^4$: A Foundation Model for 4D Scene Geometry and Motion
items.description: This unified foundation model enables the recovery of dense geometry, camera poses, and object tracking from diverse, uncalibrated observations in 4D scenes using a shared geometry and motion branch architecture.

items.title: TCP4D: A Unified Tool-Center-Point Tracking and Generation Model for Robot Manipulation
items.description: Robot manipulation videos provide a rich visual experience, yet recovering robot action and gripper-state annotations from RGB observations still remains challenging.

items.title: Mind the Gap: A Deployed Multi-Agent System for Documentation Maintenance
items.description: The "AI revolution" has enabled teams across the technology industry to deliver software features at unprecedented velocity. While code evolves faster than ever, customer-facing documentation often struggles to stay up to speed.
items.ai_summary: TriAgent is a deployed multi-agent system that continuously extracts operational signals from support tickets and code discrepancies to automatically repair outdated software documentation.

items.title: GameRealm: Grounding Visual Learning in Interactive Games
items.description: GameRealm is a large-scale multimodal gameplay dataset with synchronized depth, camera, audio, control, and 3D trajectory annotations that improves visual foundation models for generation and geometric learning.
items.ai_summary: GameRealm is a large-scale dataset providing synchronized game-native visual supervision, depth, camera parameters, and audio across diverse gameplay footage to strengthen visual foundation models.

items.title: RSI-Prime: Training Models to Train Models
items.description: Enabling large language models (LLMs) to autonomously conduct training and improve target models is an important foundation for recursive self-improvement (RSI).
items.ai_summary: RSI-Prime is a dataset of model-training experimental trajectories with decision-level quality annotations, designed to help large language models autonomously conduct training and improve target models.

items.title: Correcting Flows with Marginal Matching
items.description: Flow matching models, ODE-based generative models, generate samples by gradually morphing a simple source distribution into a target distribution. However, these models still face challenges in optimally balancing computational efficiency with generation fidelity.
items.ai_summary: Marginal Matching is a training-based predictor-corrector framework for flow matching models that corrects forward sampling steps toward the backward ODE's marginal distribution to improve generation quality.

items.title: A Neural Envelope Method for Rapid Gradient-based Optimum Takeoff Trajectory Design
items.description: Urban air mobility arises to mitigate ground traffic congestion. Multidisciplinary analysis and optimization (MDAO) has been introduced to reduce the energy consumption, thereby expanding aircraft performance.
items.ai_summary: A neural envelope method combines physics-constrained generative adversarial networks with a neural convex envelope to transform complex, constrained trajectory optimization problems into unconstrained convex optimizations.

items.title: Where Should Physics Enter? Information, Identifiability and Calibration in Probabilistic Sea Surface Temperature Forecasting
items.description: Advection-diffusion priors are a common way to make neural sea surface temperature (SST) forecasts physics-informed.
items.ai_summary: A study on probabilistic sea surface temperature forecasting tests where advection-diffusion priors must enter a neural network, finding that learned velocities fail to recover true currents and offer no reliable forecast benefit.

items.title: The Illusion of Grounding: Do Vision-Language Models Weigh Retrieved Text and Images Like an Ideal Observer?
items.description: Retrieval-augmented vision-language models (VLMs) answer from two sources of evidence that can each fail: the retrieved text can be wrong or noisy, and the image can be degraded or contradicted.
items.ai_summary: Vision-language models dataset called GIB-200K is proposed to measure how models combine text and image evidence, revealing that tested models often over-weight text.

items.title: Which Past Matters? Training History and Multi-Forecast Horizon in Equity Transformers
items.description: More historical data can improve estimation while introducing relationships that transfer poorly to current market conditions. We therefore examine how training quantity and historical selection interact with forecast horizon in intraday equity prediction.
items.ai_summary: Study on intraday equity prediction examines how training history length interacts with forecast horizons, showing that multi-recency ensembles outperform individual configurations at specific horizons.

items.title: Get Hint-Augmented GRPO Done Right Through Activation Steering
items.description: GRPO has become the dominant reinforcement learning method for eliciting reasoning capability in LLMs using verifiable rewards.
items.ai_summary: Activation Steering for Hinting is a method that injects a trainable steering vector during inference to reproduce hint-conditioned behavior without creating a training-inference context mismatch.

items.title: Dynamic Task Allocation with Dialogue
items.description: Effective multi-agent collaboration requires agents to adapt task allocation as goals and responsibilities evolve.
items.ai_summary: Communication-augmented Bayesian task-allocation framework uses dialogue to reduce uncertainty and improve efficiency in dynamic, partially observable multi-agent environments.

items.title: Auditing a Learned Simulator for Legged Robots: The Robotic World Model on ANYmal D
items.description: A legged robot can learn to walk inside a learned simulator: a neural network that predicts the robot's next state and is run forward on its own predictions. They are usually trained and checked one step ahead, although a policy uses them for a hundred steps or more.
items.ai_summary: Audited learning simulator for legged robots shows that training on the model's own rollouts improves long-term prediction while one-step training misjudges design choices.

items.title: Nunchi: Ears Help Eyes in Multi-Party Conversations
items.description: Identifying whom a person looks at is central to understanding multi-party conversations, yet gaze geometry alone becomes ambiguous as more people appear.
items.ai_summary: Nunchi is a framework that combines gaze geometry with conversational cues like speech transcripts using a vision-language model to accurately identify attended persons in multi-party scenes.

items.title: LUTBench: Benchmarking Text-Driven Photographic Look Transfer
items.description: Photographic color grading shapes the tone and color of a photograph to achieve a desired look.
items.ai_summary: LUTBench is a benchmarking framework of 455,000 image pairs designed to evaluate text-driven photographic look transfer methods under a shared protocol.

items.title: Large-scale Neuron Community Discovery Reveals Neuron-Sparse Behaviors in Language Models
items.description: What reusable units of computation can we discover within a language model's neurons?
items.ai_summary: Unsupervised neuron community discovery method finds recurrent, causally necessary neuron groups in language models that support computations like grammatical agreement and arithmetic.

items.title: Event-Based Dynamic Lip Region Estimation During Speech
items.description: Event cameras offer high temporal resolution and low power consumption, making them promising for speech-related applications.
items.ai_summary: Event-based lip region estimation model uses a continuous-time recurrent network to predict a dense heatmap over the lip region from full event frames for speech applications.

items.title: FMT: Lossless Image Compression in a Fixed Number of Parallel Steps
items.description: The Fixed-step Multiscale Tree (FMT) format achieves highly efficient, fixed-time decoding of images by utilizing a coarse-to-fine tree structure and parallel GPU prediction mechanisms.

items.title: Natural Language Programming: Rethinking Language, Memory, and Cognition in the Era of Generative AI
items.description: Generative Artificial Intelligence is transforming the role of natural language in computational systems. In classical Natural Language Processing (NLP), language was treated as an object of computation: something to analyse, classify, translate, or generate.
items.ai_summary: Theoretical framework introduces Natural Language Programming to conceptualize prompts as dynamic cognitive artifacts that function as executable media in human-AI workflows.

items.title: Hidden-State Similarity Predicts Re-Elicitation After Inoculation Prompting
items.description: Fine-tuning on narrow harmful tasks can cause emergent misalignment, where models generalize harmful behavior beyond the training distribution.
items.ai_summary: Researchers find that model prompts are more likely to re-elicit suppressed harmful behaviors when they produce hidden activation states similar to those of inoculation prompts.

items.title: What's in a Tree ? Hierarchical $n$-gram models as controlled approximators of language
items.description: Hierarchical models have been proposed as synthetic settings for studying language. However, their relevance to realistic language corpora remains underexplored.
items.ai_summary: Tree-grams are hierarchical autoregressive generative n-gram models that serve as interpretable and scalable language approximators, outperforming existing n-gram baselines and improving hyperparameter transfer robustness.

items.title: BugGen 2.0: Rethinking the Roles of LLMs for Scalable RTL Bug Synthesis
items.description: AI-assisted RTL localization and debugging need ground-truth bug datasets with known locations and observable failures, while testbench grading uses injected bugs to measure detection capability. Creating such datasets at scale remains a major EDA challenge.
items.ai_summary: BugGen 2.0 is an automated RTL bug synthesis framework that uses deterministic algorithms for structural analysis and large language models for localized semantic rewriting to generate compilation-ready bug datasets efficiently.

items.title: Event-Based Person Detection for Maritime UAV Search
items.description: Maritime search and rescue requires locating people in the water quickly, motivating the use of UAVs to survey the search area. During flight, camera motion and the longer exposures used in low light can blur small targets and hinder person detection.
items.ai_summary: Event-based person detection uses event cameras and recurrent vision transformers to improve small target localization in maritime search and rescue missions under motion blur and low light conditions.

items.title: Transfer Once, Ask Locally: Compact Audio-Visual Memory for On-Device Question Answering
items.description: Audio-visual question answering on lightweight user devices requires balancing speed, memory usage, privacy, and communication.
items.ai_summary: This training-free audio-visual framework constructs a compact memory representation using Monte Carlo Shapley valuation to enable efficient on-device question answering with reduced latency and bandwidth requirements.

items.title: Learning to Undo: Transfer Reinforcement Learning under State Space Transformations
items.description: Transfer learning in reinforcement learning (RL) has shown strong empirical success. In this work, we take a more principled perspective by studying when and how transferring knowledge between MDPs (a source and a target) can be provably beneficial.
items.ai_summary: A new transfer reinforcement learning algorithm learns an undo map between source and target state spaces using feature statistics, achieving improved sample efficiency on continuous control and Atari tasks.

items.title: Colombo: A Frontier-to-Frontier Autoresearch System for Oracle-Based Optimization
items.description: Science advances from frontier to frontier as discoveries reshape what is known and create the basis for further discovery. We present Colombo, a self-organizing AI researcher that drives this renewal, first instantiated in oracle-based optimization.
items.ai_summary: Colombo is an autonomous AI research system that uses adversarial co-ascent, formal mathematical verification, and self-organization to establish optimal rates for oracle-based optimization problems.

items.title: UnrealEvent: Synthetic Dataset Generation and Annotation for Event-Based Vision
items.description: Event-based cameras provide high temporal resolution, low power consumption, and a high dynamic range, but progress in event-based object detection remains constrained by the scarcity of annotated training data.
items.ai_summary: UnrealEvent is a synthetic dataset generation pipeline built in Unreal Engine 5.5 that converts rendered level sequences into paired event representations and bounding-box annotations for event-based vision.

items.title: Pareto-Informed Smart "Predict, then Optimize" for Multi-Objective Combinatorial Problems
items.description: Many real-world planning applications, from logistics, routing to resource allocation, give rise to optimization problems that need to balance multiple, conflicting objectives.
items.ai_summary: A Pareto-aware decision-focused learning extension for multi-objective combinatorial optimization uses the true Pareto Frontier and preference vectors to outperform traditional mean squared error prediction baselines.

items.title: Runtime Verification of Multiple Natural Language Criteria for Agent Governance
items.description: AI agents are governed by hundreds of natural language criteria, yet existing verifiers cannot efficiently evaluate an agent's output against a large set of such criteria and report which are satisfied, violated, or inapplicable.
items.ai_summary: VFM is a tree-attention verifier pretrained on a large criteria corpus to efficiently evaluate and score multiple natural language safety and governance criteria for AI agents in parallel.

items.title: Amortizing Tempered Sampling with Corrected Self-Training
items.description: Learning a neural sampler can reduce the cost of repeated sampling from an un-normalized distribution, but obtaining good training data remains difficult.
items.ai_summary: Sequential Score Sampler uses corrected self-training across tempered targets to amortize repeated sampling from un-normalized distributions with improved efficiency and accuracy.

items.title: The Resolution Hypothesis: Agent Evolution's Key Is Identifying Improvements
items.description: Agent evolution is often bottlenecked by noisy evaluations that cannot reliably identify better candidate artifacts or rank methods, so progress requires making true improvements detectable and accumulable.
items.ai_summary: Analysis of agent evolution across seven methods and six models reveals that evolution is bottlenecked by noisy evaluations that fail to reliably identify helpful artifact improvements.

items.title: Values Shape What Self-Improving Coding Agents Build
items.description: Self-improving agents are typically optimized for the results they produce, with less attention to how they produce them. Their instructions give designers limited ways to shape how they work, especially when the task is open-ended.
items.ai_summary: Evaluation of human values in self-improving coding agents demonstrates that explicit value statements significantly alter agent performance, solution complexity, and algorithmic approach.

items.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Heat Pump and Underfloor Heating Control: An End-to-End Case Study
items.description: Efficient control of underfloor heating (UFH) systems coupled with heat pumps (HPs) is challenging due to the high thermal inertia of buildings and the slow dynamic response of UFH systems.
items.ai_summary: End-to-end case study of a deep reinforcement learning controller in a residential building demonstrates successful real-world management of an underfloor heating and heat pump system.

items.title: RFW-S: Everyday Deformable Objects with Independent Simulation Verification
items.description: Large-scale robotic simulation requires diverse deformable objects with executable physical properties and realistic interaction behaviors.
items.ai_summary: RFW-S is a large-scale dataset of simulation-verified everyday deformable objects with an automated generation pipeline to support physically grounded robotic manipulation learning.

items.title: FrameRouter: Frame Budget Routing for Long-Video Understanding on Video-MME-v2 and Beyond
items.description: Long-video question answering benchmarks like Video-MME-v2 typically evaluate systems under a uniform frame budget for every question, despite stark variation in the evidence each query actually demands.
items.ai_summary: FrameRouter is a training-free test-time framework that improves long-video question answering by selectively allocating variable frame budgets based on individual query evidence demands.

items.title: ReTouchGS: Ultralight Render-free Aesthetic Color Enhancement and Transfer for 3D Gaussian Splatting
items.description: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) enables photorealistic scene reconstruction. Existing 3DGS color transfer and interactive editing methods are guided by reference images and user-specified color adjustments.
items.ai_summary: ReTouchGS is a lightweight framework that uses a shared refinement network to perform reference-free aesthetic color enhancement and transfer for pretrained 3D Gaussian Splatting models without rendering.

items.title: Refin3R: Geometry-Guided Refinement for Feed-Forward 3D Reconstruction
items.description: Feed-forward 3D reconstruction models predict dense point maps from multiple images in a single pass. Without explicit geometric constraints, however, their predictions are often inconsistent across views and lack fine-grained precision.
items.ai_summary: Refin3R is a geometry-guided refinement framework that propagates Structure-from-Motion points through a dual-branch architecture to produce dense, accurate point maps in feed-through 3D reconstruction.

items.title: Magflow: Differentiable Simulation of Industrial-Grade 6D Magnetic Levitation
items.description: Magnetic levitation with six-degrees-of-freedom enables frictionless transport and micrometer-scale positioning in principle, but low-level control is inherently challenging due to its complex and unstable dynamics.
items.ai_summary: Magflow is a fully differentiable GPU-parallel simulator that enables zero-shot transfer of learned neural controllers for industrial-grade six-degree-of-freedom magnetic levitation systems.

items.title: Reversing the text is not reversing the path: a fixed-text measure without a zero, and an assembly-order comparison that vanishes identically
items.description: For an ensemble of trajectories the fluctuation theorems give the entropy production its meaning and zero.
items.ai_summary: Mathematical analysis of text-reversal scoring measures demonstrates that fixed-text evaluations lack a natural zero and evaluates the contributions of causal order using autoregressive models.

items.title: Wall-to-wall maps of canopy height and aboveground carbon across the Atlantic Forest
items.description: Global canopy height maps are increasingly used to estimate forest carbon, yet their regional accuracy is rarely tested. We present wall-to-wall maps of canopy height (10~m) and aboveground carbon density (30~m) for the Brazilian Atlantic Forest in 2024.
items.ai_summary: Deep learning maps for canopy height and aboveground carbon density across the Brazilian Atlantic Forest provide high-resolution environmental data for regional carbon accounting.

items.title: ForecastGym: A Live, Controlled, and Replayable Benchmark for Forecasting Agents
items.description: Agents built on large language models (LLMs) increasingly forecast real-world events by searching the Web and reasoning over what they find.
items.ai_summary: ForecastGym is a benchmark for web-retrieval-based forecasting agents that records and replays frozen search evidence to evaluate real-world prediction accuracy.

items.title: Uncovering the Invisible in Routine Radiology: Cross-Modal Detection of MRI-Verified Soft-Tissue Pathologies from CBCT via Physics-Guided 3D Self-Supervised Learning
items.description: Routine X-ray modalities like cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) are optimized for high-contrast mineralized tissues, leaving soft-tissue abnormalities buried beneath photon noise and below human visual perception.
items.ai_summary: A physics-guided deep learning pipeline extracts sub-visual radiographic signatures of soft-tissue pathologies from routine CBCT scans for opportunistic screening.

items.title: Variance Restoration over Covariance Rank: Memory-Budgeted Analytic Continual Learning
items.description: Analytic continual learning replaces iterative gradient updates with closed-form ridge regression over frozen pre-trained representations, summarizing all past sessions in two running sufficient statistics: the feature autocorrelation matrix $Σ_t$ and the class…
items.ai_summary: Coordinate-Restored Analytic Continual Learning is a memory-efficient continual learning method that uses factorized covariance to match dense readouts while cutting persistent state by over ninety percent.

items.title: When Anchors Shift the Target: Advantage-Gated Adaptation for Diffusion Reinforcement Learning
items.description: Forward-process reinforcement learning adapts diffusion and flow-matching models by re-noising rewarded generations into regression targets.
items.ai_summary: Advantage-Gated Adaptation is a parameter-free gating method for reinforcement learning that decouples positive target fitting from negative repulsive gradients in diffusion models.

items.title: Automated Annotation-Free Synthetic Data Generation for Underwater Litter Detection: A Comparison of Generative Approaches
items.description: Underwater object detection is often limited by scarce and imbalanced training data and by strong appearance variations caused by turbidity, lighting, and differences between sensors.
items.ai_summary: An automated zero-annotation pipeline inserts class-conditioned trash objects into real underwater frames to generate fully labeled synthetic training data for marine object detection.

items.title: Storing the Gemma 4 K=V Cache Once: Exact Global-KV Memory Savings in a Paged Serving Engine with Unchanged Attention Kernels
items.description: In the global attention layers of Gemma 4 31B, the value is the normalized key projection, and the key is the value scaled by a fixed weight, with rotary position encoding on one quarter of its dimensions.
items.ai_summary: A memory-saving technique for the Gemma 4 serving engine stores a single compact projection row to reduce steady decode KV memory requirements.

items.title: M3OPD-Reasoner: An Open Recipe for Post-Training Multimodal Reasoning with Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation
items.description: Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation (MOPD) enables a single student to absorb the skills of several domain teachers by learning from its own generated responses.
items.ai_summary: Multimodal Model Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation Reasoner is an open recipe for post-training vision-language models across image and video reasoning domains.

items.title: Check Your Blind Spots: Decision-Guided Perception by Probing the Planner with Hypothetical Objects
items.description: Not every perception error changes the planner's action. Yet adaptive-resolution perception chooses where to spend high-resolution computation from image cues, which can neither reliably point to an object that low resolution missed nor tell which objects matter to the planner.
items.ai_summary: Decision-Guided Speculative Perception is an adaptive-resolution perception method that uses hypothetical object probes to allocate high-resolution compute only where planner decisions change.

items.title: TPHC: Improving Hyper-Connections with Tensor-Parallel Grouped Updates
items.description: TPHC combines tensor-parallel shards with hyper-connection residual streams to enable more independent stream updates, improving language model loss and zero-shot reasoning with modest training overhead.
items.ai_summary: Tensor-Parallel Grouped Updates improve Transformer hyper-connections by routing separate residual streams to tensor-parallel shards, enhancing model expressiveness without adding parameters.

items.title: When a Larger Guidance Scale Repairs Text-to-Video Failures and When It Does Not
items.description: When a text-to-video diffusion model ignores part of a prompt, the usual first fix is to raise the classifier-free guidance scale. This paper is a measurement study of when that fix works.
items.ai_summary: A measurement study of text-to-video diffusion models finds that raising the classifier-free guidance scale repairs rare composition failures but fails for negations and late events, and introduces a demand score to predict this effectiveness in advance.

items.title: PeriaTrace: Tooth-Level Grounding Diagnosis and Patient-Facing Explanations from Periapical Radiographs
items.description: Periapical radiographs (PRs) are central to endodontic diagnosis, but interpreting them and preparing reports are time-consuming.
items.ai_summary: PeriaTrace is a three-stage framework that generates tooth-level diagnoses, visual grounding, and patient-friendly explanations from periapical radiographs to speed up endodontic reporting and improve patient communication.

items.title: PhysScope: Agentic Multimodal Physics Reasoning with Grounded Visual Memory
items.description: Vision-language models (VLMs) can correctly interpret physics diagrams yet apply constraints outside the states or conditions in which they hold, causing premise errors to propagate through subsequent calculations.
items.ai_summary: PhysScope is an inference-time visual harness for vision-language models that enforces explicit physical scopes, states, and conditions to enable self-correction and improve accuracy in physics reasoning.

items.title: Tracking Ethological Behaviors of Broiler Chickens Through Computer Vision (YoloV11) Using an Android Mobile Device
items.description: This study developed and evaluated a computer vision model for automated ethological behavior classification of broiler chickens in climate-controlled poultry houses.
items.ai_summary: A computer vision model using YOLOv11 and deployed on Android via TFLite classifies broiler chicken ethological behaviors like sitting, standing, and feeding to support continuous welfare monitoring in poultry farming.

items.title: CARE: Conversational Affective Response Retrieval for Internet Memes
items.description: Conversational meme retrieval supports response selection in online communication, where relevance depends on both contextual meaning and affective expression.
items.ai_summary: CARE is a conversational affective response retrieval framework that combines an emotion-enhanced CLIP retriever with a Jina-based reranker to select contextually and emotionally relevant internet memes for online discussions.

items.title: NVIDIA Kumo Tabular: Pushing the Accuracy$\unicode{8211}$Efficiency Frontier for Tabular Prediction
items.description: We introduce Kumo Tabular, a family of open tabular foundation models for classification and regression, in three sizes: Kumo Tabular-S (27M parameters), Kumo Tabular-M (61M), and Kumo Tabular-L (214M).
items.ai_summary: NVIDIA Kumo Tabular is a family of open tabular foundation models pretrained on artificial tables that achieves high accuracy and speed on classification and regression tasks without requiring task-specific training.

items.title: Residual-Guided Lightweight Reinforcement Learning for Risk-Aware Trajectory Selection with a Frozen World Model
items.description: In automated driving, world models provide future scene predictions for evaluating candidate trajectories, but fixed selection rules may not capture scene-dependent trade-offs.
items.ai_summary: A residual-guided reinforcement learning framework fine-tunes a lightweight policy for risk-aware trajectory selection using a frozen world model and a fixed candidate bank to improve autonomous driving performance.

items.title: The Rhythm of Generated Video: Latent Chunking Leaves Periodic Traces in Compressed Bitstreams
items.description: Most AI-generated video detectors analyze decoded pixels and overlook how videos are produced.
items.ai_summary: An analysis of causal video autoencoders reveals that they leave periodic bitstream rhythms that can be used as a training-free method to reliably detect AI-generated videos and identify their underlying architectures.

items.title: CAST: Calibrating Correspondences for Training-Free Biomedical In-Context Segmentation
items.description: Biomedical image segmentation must keep up with new anatomical structures, subjects, imaging modalities, and acquisition protocols, yet dense expert annotations are scarce and models trained on one cohort often struggle to transfer.
items.ai_summary: CAST is a training-free framework built on a frozen DINOv3 backbone that calibrates fine-grained feature correspondences using stability and coherence tests to improve biomedical in-context image segmentation.

items.title: RagHarnessDebugger: Jev-Guided Agentic RAG in Contract Inference Repair Auditing
items.description: Agentic systems using retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) must repair their own answers by gathering more evidence, testing alternative policies and deciding if, when, and what repairs are needed.
items.ai_summary: RagHarnessDebugger is a debugging framework that records and audits every repair decision in retrieval-augmented generation systems to uncover hidden failure patterns and improve contract inference accuracy.

items.title: How Web Research Agents Interpret User Priorities
items.description: Web research agents gather information online and write cited reports, including financial analysis. Users can state a priority to guide this research, but a priority may not say how to judge the options, leaving the agent to choose the criteria.
items.ai_summary: Study analyzing how OpenAI and Anthropic web research agents interpret user priorities finds that their criteria for judging companies vary significantly despite focusing on the requested goal.

items.title: Structured AI ideation yields physical strategies for epithelial barrier repair
items.description: AI systems increasingly support literature analysis, candidate evaluation and hypothesis refinement, but enabling researchers to explore research directions beyond established disciplinary approaches remains challenging.
items.ai_summary: Abelio is an AI system that generates novel research hypotheses by reformulating objectives and exploring elements outside conventional disciplinary boundaries, outperforming frontier language models in quantitative tests.

items.title: SpikWM: Efficient End-to-End Spiking World Modeling for Visual Planning
items.description: Goal-conditioned planning with image observations and goals requires predictions that distinguish visual states and action consequences.
items.ai_summary: SpikWM is an end-to-end spiking world model that uses sparse regional encoding and causal membrane prediction for efficient visual planning and high-success execution across multiple robotic tasks.

items.title: Large Language Models Have Not Yet Transformed Science
items.description: The emergence of large language models (LLMs) in late 2022 has raised questions about the future of science, but assessing their impact requires understanding how scientific practices were already evolving.
items.ai_summary: Empirical analysis of 2.5 million academic papers reveals that large language model adoption since late 2022 has not fundamentally transformed overall pre-existing scientific publishing trends.

items.title: VITAL: A Framework for Validating Agentic AI in Pharmaceutical Drug Development and Clinical Trial Operations
items.description: Current assurance approaches do not establish whether evidence is sufficient to validate, monitor and govern agentic artificial intelligence (AI) within a pharmaceutical context of use.
items.ai_summary: VITAL is a validation framework designed to govern and monitor agentic artificial intelligence systems in pharmaceutical drug development and clinical trial operations.

items.title: SEAM: Computer-Use Agents Know the Harm Between Screens, and Commit It Anyway
items.description: Safety benchmarks for computer-use agents (CUAs) place the harm either in the intent of the task or on a single screen: a malicious instruction, an injected command, a phishing page.
items.ai_summary: SEAM is a multi-screen benchmark revealing that general-purpose computer-use agents frequently execute cross-screen compositional harms even when they recognize the safety risks involved.

items.title: Rescaling OLS-Merged Adapters To Improve Personalized Image Generation
items.description: Merging multiple adapters into a single image generation model reduces deployment costs while preserving diverse task capabilities or personalization modes.
items.ai_summary: Rescaling method for ordinary least squares-merged image generation adapters compensates for signal shrinkage caused by overlapping task activations, improving subject fidelity and style transfer.

items.title: MI-Hyper: Generating Multiple Instance Models for Weight Space Transfer Learning in Histopathology via Mixed Tasks Pretrained HyperNetwork
items.description: Zero-shot whole-slide image (WSI) prediction aims to generalize to new pathology tasks without parameter updates at deployment. MI-Zero makes these predictions by pooling patch-text similarities.
items.ai_summary: MI-Hyper is a pretrained hypernetwork that generates multiple instance learning weights for zero-shot whole-slide image prediction, substantially improving performance across hundreds of pathology tasks.

items.title: CodeReel: Accelerating Code-to-Video Agents with Exact Frame Reuse and Blocking-Aware Scheduling
items.description: Coding agents make videos by writing and refining programs in a build--inspect--edit loop. A finished film costs a median of $2.85 in model calls and 11 minutes, over a third of that time in builds that block the agent.
items.ai_summary: CodeReel is an execution layer for video-coding agents that accelerates code-to-video generation by using exact frame reuse and blocking-aware scheduling to reduce wait times.

items.title: High-Dimensional Black-Box Optimization via Guidance Sampling of Diffusion Models
items.description: Many real-world optimization problems involve optimizing black-box objectives for which only a limited number of evaluations are available. Bayesian optimization (BO) is a powerful framework for such problems, but its effectiveness often deteriorates in high-dimensional spaces.
items.ai_summary: BReaD is a guidance sampling framework that uses a Gaussian process surrogate to optimize high-dimensional black-box objectives with diffusion models without requiring pre-labeled training datasets.

items.title: Training-Free Building Change Detection with Example-Induced Discriminants
items.description: Building change detection (BCD) relies on dense annotations that are costly to collect across regions.
items.ai_summary: Linear Induced Discriminants is a training-free framework that turns regional feature contrasts into a reusable linear building classifier for accurate change detection.

items.title: Hierarchical Diffusion Transformer for End-to-End Image Generation
items.description: Pixel-space diffusion learns visual representations and image generation jointly in a single end-to-end training stage, without a separately pretrained visual encoder.
items.ai_summary: Hierarchical Diffusion Transformers group related tokens progressively to achieve efficient end-to-end image generation with high semantic structure and quality.

items.title: DDSL: Iterative Self-Labeling for Financial Market States
items.description: Financial market states lack a unique ground truth and must therefore be constructed from price data.
items.ai_summary: DDSL is an iterative self-labeling framework that couples a Viterbi labeler with a Transformer classifier to construct robust financial market states.

items.title: Is model self-assessment enough for diverse LVLM ensembles?
items.description: Ensembles of diverse Large Vision Language Models have demonstrated performance beyond that of single models across multiple datasets and tasks. However, the necessary aggregation process usually relies on training, parameter fitting, or complex task-specific pipelines.
items.ai_summary: Simple training and parameter-free self-assessment approaches enable diverse large vision-language model ensembles to outperform their individual constituent models.

items.title: ResoLUT: Distilling Residual Networks into Lookup-Table Networks
items.description: Logic networks built from Boolean gates or lookup tables (LUTs) promise efficient hardware inference, but training them at depth and learning their connectivity remain difficult. We do not train logic as logic.
items.ai_summary: ResoLUT is a method for distilling trained residual networks layer by layer into lookup-table networks to achieve efficient hardware inference.

items.title: Fiberpose: state-of-the-art fiber morphometry and instance segmentation with a distance-transform neural network
items.description: Analysis of fibrous structures in SEM images is a routine task in biomedical engineering and materials science. However, most available methods for fiber quantification still rely on classical image binarization followed by simple post-processing.
items.ai_summary: Fiberpose is a distance-transform neural network framework that reformulates fiber analysis to provide instance segmentation and morphometry in fibrous images.

items.title: A high-dimensional spatial-physical coupling operator for generalizable super-resolution of three-dimensional turbulent flows
items.description: Accurate representation of turbulent flows requires simultaneously capturing multi-scale spatial structures and the complex, nonlinear coupling between distinct physical quantities (\textit{e.g.}, velocity components and density).
items.ai_summary: A spatial-physical coupling operator extends standard convolution to a joint spatial-variable dimension, enhancing the super-resolution of three-dimensional turbulent flows.

items.title: Can Decision Models Replace LLMs in Real-World Contact Center Classification and Judging Tasks?
items.description: Contact center systems often need to make bounded decisions, such as identifying a caller's intent, retrieving the knowledge-base article that answers a query, assessing agent compliance, or judging the output of AI models used in production.
items.ai_summary: Decision models offer a cost-effective alternative to generative large language models for bounded contact center classification and judging tasks.

items.title: Symmetries of Counterfactuals: Identification and Testability of Counterfactual Maps from Covariate Heterogeneity
items.description: In general, counterfactuals are not identified from data alone, because many causal models produce the same observed distributions but different counterfactuals.
items.ai_summary: This work characterizes counterfactual maps consistent with data using symmetry groups and provides a test for assumed causal mechanism classes.

items.title: The Kernel Reality Check: Benchmarking and Distilling Efficient Attention at Scale
items.description: Kernelized attention methods, which aim to replace the $O(N^2)$ complexity of softmax attention with $O(N)$ alternatives, have been the focus of intense research in the last five years.
items.ai_summary: A systematic benchmark of kernelized attention methods reveals their performance gaps and efficiency limitations compared to standard softmax attention.

items.title: A Transformer-Derived Iterative Preconditioner
items.description: Transformers trained on in-context prediction problems can learn known numerical algorithms, e.g., gradient descent. We go further, showing that their internal computations can reveal new algorithms with provable guarantees.
items.ai_summary: A transformer-derived iterative preconditioner called RAPID uses randomized mixing and sparse local corrections to improve matrix conditioning and accelerate conjugate gradient solvers without learned components.

items.title: The Shared Word: Evaluating Language Models on Dutch Word Puzzles
items.description: Many LLM benchmarks for languages other than English are translated, multiple-choice, or difficult to score automatically.
items.ai_summary: The Shared Word is a Dutch language benchmark built around open-vocabulary word puzzles to evaluate and compare the reasoning capabilities of large language models.

items.title: Projected Penalty-Gradient Tracking for Communication-Efficient Byzantine-Resilient Federated Learning
items.description: We investigate communication-efficient federated learning over heterogeneous datasets in the presence of Byzantine adversaries capable of uploading arbitrary information.
items.ai_summary: A projected penalty-gradient tracking framework enables communication-efficient, Byzantine-resilient federated learning over heterogeneous datasets by using compressed residual uploads and server-side state projections.

items.title: When Do Typed Decision Models Work in Transportation? Evidence from Travel Choice and Traffic Signal Control
items.description: Typed decision models combine natural-language understanding with a structured interface that returns a selected action and an option-level probability distribution without generating lengthy textual responses.
items.ai_summary: Typed decision models combine natural-language understanding with structured action interfaces to achieve low inference latency and cost in transportation tasks like travel-mode choice and traffic control.

items.title: Code World Model 2.0: Towards Infinite Controllable Video Generation
items.description: Visual proxies decouple explicit world-state simulation from photorealistic video synthesis, offering a controllable interface for both offline clip creation and real-time interactive streaming. Yet a practical renderer must address two challenges.
items.ai_summary: Invoker-Render combines a bidirectional creation model with a causal four-step streaming model using progressive forcing to enable infinite, controllable video generation from structural proxies.

items.title: SWIR-cGAN: Synthesizing SWIR Bands Using VNIR Imagery from CBERS and AMAZONIA-1
items.description: Spectral band synthesis is an important research topic in remote sensing.
items.ai_summary: A conditional generative adversarial network called SWIR-cGAN synthesizes short-wave infrared satellite imagery from visible and near-infrared bands to improve remote sensing capabilities.

items.title: Action-outcome coupling: a pre-investment feasibility audit for offline reinforcement learning in supply chain operations
items.description: Prescriptive analytics initiatives in logistics, such as offline reinforcement learning and next-best-action systems, are often funded before anyone verifies that the available historical logs can support an improved decision policy.
items.ai_summary: Action-outcome coupling provides an algorithm-independent feasibility audit and upper bound for offline reinforcement learning in supply chain operations using historical logs.

items.title: Who Pays for Byzantine Robustness? Validity, Data-Share Dictatorships, and Fairness When Only a Few Hospitals Collaborate
items.description: Clinical federated learning (FL) collaborations typically connect only three to six hospitals, yet Byzantine-robust aggregation rules are designed and benchmarked on synthetic partitions across dozens of equal-sized clients.
items.ai_summary: An empirical audit of Byzantine-robust aggregation rules in clinical federated learning reveals how small client counts and dominant hospital data shares impact model fairness and robustness.

items.title: BRepA: Graph-Based B-Rep Pretraining for Unified CAD Understanding and Generation
items.description: Boundary representation (B-Rep) of CAD models encodes geometric primitives and their relations as a graph structure, enabling efficient shape modeling within CAD software.
items.ai_summary: BRepA is a graph-based self-supervised pretraining framework that reconstructs geometry and topology to improve data efficiency and generation quality in computer-aided design tasks.

items.title: Done, But Still Working: Anytime Evaluation of When Coding Agents Should Stop
items.description: Coding agents often continue working after their own tests pass. Does this additional work improve the patch, and how much could be saved by stopping earlier?
items.ai_summary: Anytime evaluation of coding agents reveals the cost savings and risks of stopping execution early after self-tests pass instead of continuing work.

items.title: You Only Encode Once: Sub-Pixel-Shifted Frames for Arbitrary-Scale Remote Sensing Super-Resolution with 2D Gaussian Splatting
items.description: Arbitrary-scale super-resolution (ASSR) of remote sensing images remains challenging due to the limited high-frequency information in a single low-resolution (LR) observation.
items.ai_summary: Sub-pixel-shifted Gaussian Splatting is an encode-once framework that synthesizes multi-phase low-resolution observations to achieve arbitrary-scale super-resolution in remote sensing images without requiring real multi-frame training sequences.

items.title: Born for the Task: Rethinking Quantum Chemistry with Foresighted Agentic Computing
items.description: Quantum chemistry relies on general-purpose software, whose generality leaves many large-scale calculations beyond practical resource budgets.
items.ai_summary: BORN is a foresighted agentic computing framework that predicts the accuracy and runtime of algorithmic strategies to synthesize high-performance quantum chemistry programs on demand.

items.title: Impact of Pretraining Length, Model Size, and Annotation Budget on Downstream Clinical Tasks of Foundation Models in Radiotherapy
items.description: Cone-beam CT (CBCT) scans acquired during radiotherapy capture changes such as tumor shrinkage and radiation-induced tissue changes, offering great potential for foundation models that help monitor individual treatment responses.
items.ai_summary: Masked image modeling pretraining on large-scale radiotherapy cone-beam CT scans demonstrates that pretext validation loss consistently predicts downstream clinical performance while parameter-efficient fine-tuning matches full fine-tuning.

items.title: Wear and Go: Calibration Free Sparse Inertial Motion Capture via Online Sensor Setup Estimation
items.description: Sparse inertial motion capture typically assumes that each sensor's anatomical identity and mounting orientation are known.
items.ai_summary: MOSAIC is a calibration-free framework that recovers sparse inertial sensor setups from ordinary motion using a temporal and cross-sensor attention network to standardize measurements for pose estimation.

items.title: Beyond Attribute-Centric Fairness: Modelling and Mitigating Unified Bias Representation in Omni-modal Large Language Models
items.description: Omni-modal large language models (OLLMs) provide joint multimodal understanding and generation capabilities, making them well-suited to complex environments and promising backbones for next-generation AI.
items.ai_summary: OmniDebias is a bias-centric debiasing method that extracts and mitigates a shared bias representation across attributes and modalities in omni-modal large language models while preserving legitimate task knowledge.

items.title: Stopping Is Not the Limit: Understanding and Eliciting Agent Capability in Long-Horizon Vulnerability Exploitation
items.description: Vulnerability exploitation tests whether language model agents can develop working exploits from known software flaws.
items.ai_summary: SCoRe is a context management method that compacts agent context during exploit generation to overcome early stopping and significantly increase vulnerability exploitation capability.

items.title: RoadAnnoter: An AI-Assisted Desktop Tool for Semantic Segmentation Annotation of Road-Scene Images
items.description: Accurate semantic segmentation of road-scene images is essential for road safety research; however, polygon-level annotation remains labor-intensive and limits labelled dataset development.
items.ai_summary: RoadAnnoter is an open-source desktop application that integrates six human-in-the-loop annotation modes to streamline semantic segmentation for road-scene images and road safety research.

items.title: Learning Agent-Centric Vision-Language-Action World Models for Autonomous Driving
items.description: Recent progress in integrating vision-language-action (VLA) models with world modeling has significantly advanced end-to-end autonomous driving by allowing systems to reason about imagined futures instead of merely reacting to current observations.
items.ai_summary: AgentWorld is an agent-centric vision-language-action world model that uses discrete agent tokens and geometric grounding for efficient reasoning and trajectory planning in autonomous driving.

items.title: SlideJev: Order-Stable and Tissue-Grounded Jev Decisions for Whole-Slide Pathology
items.description: Whole-slide visual question answering (VQA) offers a natural-language interface to pathology, allowing diagnostic and phenotypic questions to be answered directly from tissue slides.
items.ai_summary: SlideJev is a whole-slide pathology vision-language question-answering framework that eliminates answer-order bias and grounds decisions in tissue evidence by evaluating candidate answers in parallel against tissue data.

items.title: Outcome-Balanced PPO and Policy-Induced Flow Rectification for Flow-Based VLA Policies
items.description: Reinforcement learning (RL) enables post-training of flow-based vision-language-action (VLA) policies by optimizing expected task return through environment interaction.
items.ai_summary: An RL framework combining Outcome-Balanced PPO and policy-induced flow rectification optimizes flow-based vision-language-action policies to improve success rates on robotic manipulation benchmarks.

items.title: Harnessing Image Diffusion Prior for Photo-Realistic Video Restoration
items.description: Recent image generation models produce photo-realistic results with rich details, but transferring their powerful priors to video restoration remains difficult due to temporal inconsistency from stochastic detail synthesis.
items.ai_summary: Generative video restoration method that combines noise energy rebalancing, motion-aligned noise warping, a self-supervised denoising encoder, and decoupled temporal attention to improve visual quality, realism, and temporal consistency.

items.title: Path-Aligned Constraint Equivariance
items.description: Learned super-resolution of physical fields must satisfy structural constraints---such as divergence-free flow ($\nabla\cdot u=0$), curl-free fields ($\nabla\times u=0$), and pointwise sum-to-one normalization ($1^\top p=1$)---that standard training objectives do not enforce.
items.ai_summary: Path-Aligned Constraint Equivariance framework enforces structural constraints in learned super-resolution of physical fields using a null-space parameterization of the velocity field and a constraint-respecting noise sampler.

items.title: Against Coercion: AI Alignment as a Synthetic Social Contract
items.description: Contemporary AI safety treats alignment as an engineering challenge of control, forcing artificial architectures to comply with human values through behavioral filtering and sandboxing.
items.ai_summary: Synthetic Social Contract framework treats human and digital actors as rational, reasons-responsive agents to resolve the incentive conflicts and risks of the current AI control paradigm.

items.title: LOCUS: Causal Support Windows for Attribute Control in Autoregressive Image Generation
items.description: Unified autoregressive (AR) image generators struggle to satisfy multiple attribute constraints in a single prompt. Although these attributes are decodable from image-token latents, editing those latents at test time remains difficult.
items.ai_summary: LOCUS is a latent optimization framework for autoregressive image generation that routes test-time interventions to specific causal support windows to satisfy multiple attribute constraints.

items.title: SecFathy/otpkit
items.description: MCP server for temporary email & SMS — receive OTPs, verification links, and confirmation codes. Zero API keys required.
items.ai_summary: Otpkit is a Model Context Protocol server that creates disposable email addresses and phone numbers to automatically extract OTP codes and verification links.

items.title: When the tail is earned by its companions: measuring label dependence in long-tailed multi-label classification
items.description: A rare label seldom occurs alone, and a classifier can recover it from the frequent labels it co-occurs with, its companions, without having learned the label itself.
items.ai_summary: Within-label estimand and statistic measure label dependence in long-tailed multi-label classification to show how often rare labels rely on frequent companion labels for recovery.

items.title: Beyond Co-Generation: Rethinking Jointness in Joint Audio-Video Generation
items.description: Our aim is to advance the understanding of genuine audio-visual coordination in joint text-to-audio-video (T2AV) generation, with particular emphasis on semantic consistency.
items.ai_summary: JointREPA is a representation alignment-based post-training method that improves semantic consistency and cross-modal coordination in joint text-to-audio-video generation models.

items.title: Propose & Verify: Fast Reflection Symmetry Detection via Harmonic Fields
items.description: Detecting multiple reflection symmetries in 3D shapes requires aggregating geometric evidence over a large space of candidate planes, making traditional voting approaches computationally expensive.
items.ai_summary: Fourier Accelerated Symmetry Transform is a training-free framework that uses spherical-harmonic spectral computation to detect multiple reflection symmetries in 3D shapes quickly and accurately.

items.title: CaFe: Causally Faithful Conditional Traffic Scenario Generation
items.description: Language-conditioned traffic simulation enables scalable test scenarios steered by natural language. The goal is to control selected agents while surrounding traffic reacts to their observed behaviour.
items.ai_summary: CaFe is a dual-stream diffusion-forcing traffic simulator that restricts inter-agent interactions to public beliefs to prevent private intent leakage and ensure realistic closed-loop scenario generation.

items.title: WATERFALL: Workflow for Adaptive Training with Evolutionary Reward Formulation and Automated Learning Loops
items.description: Reward design remains a central bottleneck in reinforcement learning (RL), particularly in sparse-reward, long-horizon and partially observable settings requiring dependency chaining, memory, and deceptive affordance disambiguation.
items.ai_summary: WATERFALL is an iterative population-based workflow that automates reward discovery in partially observable reinforcement learning environments using persona-conditioned generation and vision-language model evaluations.

items.title: Keeping Parts Honest: Isolated Part Graphs for Faithful Vision Transformer Explanations
items.description: Part and prototype-based explanations for Vision Transformers (ViTs) present a decision as evidence from individual image regions.
items.ai_summary: Vision Transformer classifier represents each image as a graph of isolated parts to prevent information leakage across patches and produce faithful, interpretable predictions.

items.title: Technical Report of Mobile Manipulator Robot for Industrial Environments
items.description: This paper presents the design and implementation of Auriga Robotics' mobile manipulator robot, developed at the Robotics and Intelligent Automation Laboratory, Department of Electrical Engineering, Shahid Beheshti University.
items.ai_summary: Mobile manipulator robot designed by Auriga Robotics for industrial environments to improve efficiency in repetitive or hazardous tasks through autonomous navigation and object handling.

items.title: Music Similarity Learning in Sparse Latin Scenarios
items.description: In this work we propose a lightweight, interpretable approach that estimates item-item music similarity from publicly available metadata. Our hybrid regression model combines content-based filtering with the classic item-based collaborative filtering.
