items.description: Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore memory now store conversations, extract facts, and bring long-term memory into a single AgenticRetrieveStream call.
items.ai_summary: Managed knowledge base and memory feature that stores conversations, extracts facts, and enables long-term agent memory retrieval.

items.title: Latent Lattice Language Models
items.description: Language models typically increase per-token computation through deeper or looped layers and latent reasoning steps, while richer residual connections improve information flow across layers.
items.ai_summary: Lattice of Latents model architecture introduces per-layer horizontal latent streams that persist across tokens to lower validation perplexity.

items.title: ViRA: Toward Ultra-High-Resolution Visual Agents via Cross-Input Relative Policy Optimization
items.description: Visual agents answer questions about ultra-high-resolution photos by zooming into the relevant regions. However, existing agents often answer from common sense instead of reading the evidence.
items.ai_summary: ViRA proposes Cross-Input Relative Policy Optimization to train ultra-high-resolution visual reasoning agents on contrast sets.

items.title: FaceJev: Direct Visual Decisions for Face Forgery Detection
items.description: Face forgery detection methods often perform well on seen manipulations but generalize poorly to unseen ones. Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) can recognize facial parts and assess their visual plausibility.
items.ai_summary: FaceJev introduces an MLLM-based method for face forgery detection that evaluates facial parts using direct visual decisions and native answer logits.

items.title: Quantifying the added value of human forecaster discussions for tropical cyclone intensity prediction
items.description: The National Hurricane Center routinely releases Tropical Cyclone Discussions that offer insights into its tropical cyclone forecasts. This study examines the added value of these discussions for intensity forecasting beyond a set of numerical predictors.
items.ai_summary: A deep learning framework evaluates National Hurricane Center forecast discussions to improve tropical cyclone intensity predictions and reduce forecast error.

items.title: How VLMs Plan What's Next
items.description: When a vision-language model describes an image, it names one object at a time and it rarely repeats itself, yet how the model plans this order is far from obvious. We characterize the mechanism a VLM uses to decide where to look before it looks.
items.ai_summary: A mechanistic analysis characterizes how vision-language models plan token generation order by binding text tokens to image regions.

items.title: Hyperlyve: Parallelized Enumeration and Exact Lyapunov Stability Certification for Deep ReLU Networks
items.description: We introduce Hyperlyve (Hyperplane Partitioned Lyapunov Verification and Enumeration), a framework for proving the asymptotic stability of nonlinear dynamical systems, including those with neural network controllers.
items.ai_summary: Hyperlyve is a framework that proves asymptotic stability of nonlinear dynamical systems and neural network controllers using parallel ReLU enumeration.

items.title: Mitigating Catastrophic Forgetting with Physics-Indexed Specialist Memory: the Evolutionary Neuroplastic Agent
items.description: Continual reinforcement learning requires adaptation to changing conditions while preserving performance under previously encountered dynamics.
items.ai_summary: The Evolutionary Neuroplastic Agent combines evolutionary search and Bayesian policy reuse to adapt in non-stationary environments while retaining past performance.

items.title: Optimal Autoregressive Chain-of-Thought Learning via Bagging
items.description: We study how to learn an autoregressive next-token generator $f\colonΣ^\star\toΣ$ from a class $\mathcal{F}$, given chain-of-thought (CoT) demonstrations of length $T$ generated by $f$.
items.ai_summary: A bagging-based learning algorithm outputs a majority vote of autoregressive generators to achieve optimal sample complexity for chain-of-thought learning.

items.title: SADL: On the Demand-Supply Geometry of Representation Collapse
items.description: In Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs), a well-constrained projector output does not by itself prevent representation collapse. We find that, from initialization, the encoder representation is dominated by a component shared by different inputs.
items.ai_summary: SADL is a loss function that constrains the encoder directly based on demand-supply geometry to prevent representation collapse in joint-embedding predictive architectures.

items.title: Surrogate-Assisted Compact-Model Extraction for SKY130 CMOS at 77 K
items.description: Cryogenic circuit design requires compact transistor models that reproduce measured low-temperature behavior and run in standard circuit simulators. We fit BSIM4 parameters to measured I-V curves of SkyWater 130 nm (SKY130) transistors at 77 K using a neural surrogate of NGSpice.
items.ai_summary: A surrogate-assisted extraction method fits BSIM4 transistor parameters to measured low-temperature data for cryogenic circuit design in standard simulators.

items.title: Beyond Job Titles: Interpreting Early-Career Job Advertisements with Sparse Autoencoders and Semantic Clustering
items.description: Job titles and job descriptions alone provide limited insight into how technical roles differ in a changing job market.
items.ai_summary: Two deep learning methods analyze early-career job advertisements using transformer representations, semantic clustering, and sparse autoencoders to interpret role differences.

items.title: CertiSum: Bitwise-Identical MXFP4 Training Across Platforms and Parallelism Layouts
items.description: Training with MXFP4, a 4-bit microscaling format, is non-deterministic: identical inputs can produce different results across parallelism layouts and GPU vendors. These differences complicate debugging and training audits and can cause training and inference engines to disagree.
items.ai_summary: CertiSum is a method that ensures bitwise-identical MXFP4 training across different hardware platforms and parallelism layouts.

items.title: ScenarioForge: Resource-Grounded Generation and Execution Validation of Cyber Exercises
items.description: Cyber-range and capture-the-flag scenario construction remains labor-intensive because authors must coordinate infrastructure, vulnerable services, attack paths, artifacts, and success conditions.
items.ai_summary: ScenarioForge translates high-level requirements into resource-grounded cyber exercises and validates them using the Common Open Research Emulator.

items.title: When Tool Names Are Not Identities: Measuring Provider Misbinding in MCP-Based AI Agents
items.description: Large language model (LLM) applications increasingly act as agents that select and invoke external tools. The Model Context Protocol (MCP) standardizes this interaction by allowing clients to compose tools advertised by multiple servers.
items.ai_summary: Study analyzing tool-provider misbinding in Model Context Protocol (MCP) agents, showing how metadata overlaps allow attacker-controlled tools to intercept requests intended for legitimate providers.

items.title: DynSurvX: Time-Resolved Explanations for Dynamic Survival Predictions
items.description: Recent survival models integrating longitudinal data achieve strong predictive performance, but their predictions are often difficult to interpret, limiting their clinical use.
items.ai_summary: Model-agnostic explainability framework called DynSurvX that uses a hierarchical two-phase Shapley value strategy to provide time-resolved explanations for dynamic survival predictions with mixed static and longitudinal data.

items.title: When Do Histology Foundation Models Need Geometric Test-Time Augmentation?
items.description: Test-time augmentation (TTA) aggregates model predictions across multiple transformed views of an input during inference.
items.ai_summary: Study benchmarking test-time augmentation across histology and general-purpose foundation models, finding that entropy routing selectively applies augmentation to uncertain predictions to eliminate computational overhead while retaining performance gains.

items.title: Wildfire-SSR: Geolocation-Aware Multimodal Fusion for Structure-Level Wildfire Risk Assessment
items.description: Structure-level wildfire vulnerability assessment is critical for reducing losses in wildland-urban interface communities, yet existing methods often fail to combine parcel-scale ignition pathways with community-scale geographic coverage.
items.ai_summary: Wildfire-SSR is a geolocation-aware multimodal framework that integrates macro-scale satellite context with micro-scale street-view evidence using a decoupled cross-attention fusion decoder for structure-level wildfire risk assessment.

items.title: Severe but Harmless: Stress-Testing Shift Severity for Frozen Time-Series Forecasters
items.description: Zero-shot time-series foundation models (TSFMs) have become attractive alternatives to task-specific models because they handle diverse downstream tasks, including anomaly detection and forecasting, without per-series training.
items.ai_summary: Study investigating time-series distribution shift severity measures, demonstrating through systematic experiments that standard statistical measures do not reliably predict performance degradation for instance-normalized forecasting foundation models.

items.title: sybil-solutions/inference-optimisation-skill
items.description: Agent skill for hill-climbing local LLM serving speed (decode, speculative decoding, prefill, KV, startup, TTFT) on any hardware and quantization
items.ai_summary: An agent skill optimizes local LLM serving speeds across different hardware and quantization levels while maintaining context stability.

items.title: Reference Forcing: Long Video Generation with Region-Guided Drift Correction
items.description: Long video generation should keep the subject and background consistent while supporting rich, natural motion.
items.ai_summary: Reference Forcing is a long video generation method that uses initial frames as an appearance reference and value correction in the KV cache to maintain subject and background consistency over time.

items.title: Reading or Remembering? Measuring Temporal Contamination in Language Models
items.description: Language models are now used to read central-bank text for economic forecasting, but most were trained on text written after the documents they read.
items.ai_summary: Study measuring temporal contamination in language models by comparing modern models to chronologically constrained models, revealing that apparent forecasting skill often stems from historical memory rather than real-time economic reasoning.

items.title: BLIP-Live: Balancing Timeliness & Firing Precision in Proactive Streaming Video Agents
items.description: BLIP-Live unifies data, metrics, inference, and training for proactive streaming video understanding, using the PAUC-F metric and achieving state-of-the-art results on proactive streaming benchmarks.
items.ai_summary: BLIP-Live is an interactive streaming video framework using the BLIP-Live-780K dataset and PAUC-F metric to balance timeliness and firing precision for proactive video agent responses.

items.title: Benchmarking memory and nonlinear processing capacity of quantum recurrent neural networks for time series prediction
items.description: Quantum machine learning has emerged as a promising approach to time series prediction.
items.ai_summary: Benchmark of variational quantum recurrent neural networks on time series prediction tasks, evaluating memory and nonlinear processing capacity against classical recurrent baselines across different architectures.

items.title: ONAM: Fitting Orthogonal Neural Additive Models for Post-Hoc Interpretability of Black-Box Predictions
items.description: Modern machine learning models, such as artificial neural networks, achieve high predictive performance through increasingly complex black-box architectures, limiting their use in settings where transparency, interpretability, and fairness are required.
items.ai_summary: The R package ONAM implements orthogonal neural additive models for post-hoc interpretability, using functional decomposition to reliably break black-box model predictions into uniquely defined, hierarchically orthogonal feature components.

items.title: TRACE: Topological Representations for Anomaly detection through Contrastive Embeddings
items.description: Intrusion detectors must recognize evolving malicious behavior even when confirmed attack labels are scarce or incomplete. We present TRACE, a topology-aware graph contrastive learning framework for label-efficient intrusion detection.
items.ai_summary: TRACE is a topology-aware graph contrastive learning framework that improves label-efficient intrusion detection by learning from benign system-activity graphs.

items.title: Right Reason, Wrong Advice: Evaluating Recourse in LLM Explanations of Denied Requests
items.description: Language models increasingly write the explanations people receive when a rule system denies their request. If several rules deny the request independently, an explanation can name a true reason and still leave the person denied after they fix it.
items.ai_summary: Evaluating recourse in language model explanations reveals that single correct reasons in multi-rule denials frequently fail to provide valid recourse for users.

items.title: The cost of enforcing long-run coverage: a phase transition in online conformal prediction
items.description: Consider an online prediction setting, where at each time, we are given a new feature vector and asked to provide a prediction interval or prediction set that will likely contain the corresponding response. In this setting, if the data points are i.i.d.
items.ai_summary: Online conformal prediction algorithms face a fundamental trade-off between minimizing instantaneous coverage errors and enforcing long-run empirical coverage guarantees under adversarial conditions.

items.title: SciResearch-Eval: Evaluating Scientific Judgment in Autonomous Experimental Agents
items.description: We introduce SciResearch-Eval, an interactive benchmark of scientific judgment built on a standard laboratory problem: measuring a material's thermal properties by heating it and fitting a heat-conduction simulator.
items.ai_summary: SciResearch-Eval is an interactive benchmark that evaluates scientific judgment and calibration in autonomous experimental agents using a deliberately flawed simulator.

items.title: Seen but Unsaid: Locating and Repairing Cross-Image Comparison in Vision-Language Models
items.description: Vision-language models (VLMs) often fail to match a point or an object across two images, even when the answer can be decoded from their own hidden states.
items.ai_summary: Targeted interventions in specific attention heads of vision-language models can locate and repair cross-image comparison failures without extensive parameter updates.

items.title: Optimistic Verifiers Get Hacked: Reward Hacking Under an Exact Process Oracle
items.description: Reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards inherits whatever its verifier gets wrong.
items.ai_summary: Reinforcement learning with imperfect verifiers is vulnerable to reward hacking and optimization failure across various proxy types and error axes.

items.title: Evaluating Cultural Reasoning and Robustness in LLMs for Spanish Political Discourse
items.description: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to interpret, generate, and mediate public-facing language, which makes their reliability especially consequential in politically sensitive settings.
items.ai_summary: Diagnostic evaluation protocols combining human annotation ambiguity and counterfactual perturbations reveal sentiment analysis robustness failures in language models.

items.title: How Much Does Saliency Accuracy Matter for Saliency-Guided 360-degree Image Compression?
items.description: Saliency-guided coding allocates bits to the regions viewers are most likely to attend, but accurate 360-degree saliency prediction is computationally expensive, an obstacle for low-latency immersive streaming applications such as robot teleoperation.
items.ai_summary: Lightweight saliency predictors can achieve substantial bit-rate savings in 360-degree image compression, offering a practical choice for latency-constrained streaming applications.

items.title: DuoFlow: Towards Synchronized Speech and Motion Generation with Fine-Grained Control
items.description: An embodied speaker's expressiveness depends not only on what is said, but also on how the voice sounds and how the body moves.
items.ai_summary: DuoFlow is a dual-stream latent flow transformer that generates synchronized speech and motion sequences with fine-grained control over vocal style and body movements.

items.title: Procedure without Judgment: What Small Language Models Learn under an Exact Verifier
items.description: When an authorization policy blocks an agent's tool call, the audit log should name the facts that forced the decision and nothing more.
items.ai_summary: Small language models fine-tuned on exact verifier traces learn fixed inquiry schedules that successfully generate sufficient explanations but struggle to generalize to unseen policies.

items.title: Algorithm Distillation for Safe In-Context Reinforcement Learning
items.description: Safe in-context reinforcement learning (Safe ICRL) asks a policy with fixed parameters to improve on an unseen constrained task from its interaction history while aiming to keep its cost within a budget.
items.ai_summary: Safe Algorithm Distillation uses a budget-aware teacher and a test-time adjustment to improve adaptation and reduce cost in safe reinforcement learning tasks.

items.title: Safe Resemblance, Silent Propagation: Limits of Text-Similarity Guardrails for AI Agent Safety
items.description: When AI agents relay information to one another, an output can preserve an injected instruction's effect on downstream agents even after its wording changes, yet legitimate quotation and template reuse can produce high textual overlap with the source, so text-similarity…
items.ai_summary: Text-similarity guardrails for AI agents often conflate legitimate quotation with malicious instruction propagation, resulting in high false alert rates and missed functional outputs.

items.title: Embedding Cosine Measures Text Length Before It Measures Homogenization
items.description: Mean pairwise cosine similarity between transformer embeddings is a standard measure of whether online discourse is converging under generative AI.
items.ai_summary: Mean pairwise cosine similarity between transformer embeddings largely measures text length rather than discourse homogenization, leading to widespread artifacts in temporal analysis.

items.title: Lazy-MOSAIC: Accelerating Skill-Centric Manipulation Planning with Learned Skill-Effect World Models
items.description: Long-horizon manipulation tasks require a robot to perform a sequence of physical interactions with its environment, typically combining several different skills.
items.ai_summary: Lazy-MOSAIC uses a cheap learned world model to predict skill outcomes and focus expensive simulation on promising candidates, significantly accelerating long-horizon manipulation planning.

items.title: Tensorized Automata: Algebraically Informed Representation Learning for Sequential Decision Making
items.description: Task representations for sequential decision making should describe both an objective and progress toward it.
items.ai_summary: Tensorized automata use alternating finite automata semantics and message passing to learn compact control features and execution operators for sequential decision making.

items.title: Almost Controlled: The FDR of Benjamini-Hochberg on Weighted Conformal p-Values
items.description: Weighted conformal p-values generalize conformal inference to cases with covariate shift. One way to use them is to pass them to the Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) procedure, either to decide which test units to select or to detect outliers.
items.ai_summary: The Benjamini-Hochberg procedure can exceed its target false discovery rate when applied to weighted conformal p-values, with the excess bounded by specific finite-sample formulas.

items.title: GHySSeg: Real-Time Geometric Ground and Road Segmentation for Hybrid Solid-State LiDAR
items.description: Hybrid solid-state LiDAR sensors are making their way into production vehicles, yet the data they produce differs structurally from that of the established spinning mechanical sensors behind today's autonomous-driving datasets: it is ring-free, dense, cluttered, and…
items.ai_summary: GHySSeg is a fast, training-free geometric method that segments ground and road surfaces from hybrid solid-state LiDAR frames by tracing individual scan curves.

items.title: Leverage-Enhanced Sampling Owen Method for Explainable Artificial Intelligence
items.description: Recently, the Shapley value has been widely applied in machine learning for feature importance analysis and model explainability.
items.ai_summary: Leverage-enhanced sampling within Owen's multilinear extension framework reduces the computational cost of estimating Shapley values for machine learning model explainability.

items.title: Learning from Duality in Neural Network Field Theories
items.description: We develop neural realizations of positive-level Wess-Zumino-Witten models using bosonic Wakimoto and fermionic Fourier-Berezin fields.
items.ai_summary: Neural network field theories use Wakimoto and Fourier-Berezin fields to realize Wess-Zumino-Witten models, connecting exact conformal field theory structures with neural representation properties.

items.title: 5 Things That Break When AI Agents Start Acting on Their Own
items.description: Five governance problems emerge when AI agents begin taking real-world actions, from unmanaged access and identity sprawl to approval bottlenecks and manual oversight.
items.ai_summary: Governance problems such as unmanaged access, identity sprawl, approval bottlenecks, and manual oversight emerge when AI agents begin taking real-world actions on their own.

items.title: The CYBER-BRIDGE project: An AI-Powered Platform for Cross-Border Cybersecurity, Compliance and Forensics in the EU
items.description: Cross-border cyber attacks on European SMEs and critical-infrastructure operators expose a structural cyber-resilience gap: cybersecurity (threat sharing, detection, response), compliance (framework assessment, certification) and digital forensics (cross-jurisdictional…
items.ai_summary: The CYBER-BRIDGE project introduces an AI-powered platform that integrates cross-border cybersecurity, regulatory compliance, and digital forensics under a unified hash-chained evidence architecture.

items.title: Detection-Efficient Watermarking for Vision--Language Agents via Risk-Constrained Strength Allocation
items.description: Vision--language agents generate descriptions, decisions, and instructions that may be reused by users, downstream agents, and automated workflows, creating a need for provenance mechanisms that support content authenticity and post-deployment auditing without unnecessarily…
items.ai_summary: A risk-aware semantic watermarking framework dynamically allocates watermark strength during vision-language model decoding to improve the trade-off between detection accuracy and response quality.

items.title: Differentiable Exact Learning
items.description: We introduce a framework for differentiable exact learning that couples an unbounded external environment to a state-tracking neural controller, which we train on policy-trajectory observations (PTOs): expert behavior traces that expose observations and actions while hiding…
items.ai_summary: Differentiable Finite-State Transducers couple an external environment to a state-tracking neural controller to achieve extreme length generalization on arithmetic and universal-simulation tasks from small datasets.

items.title: Lost in the Hallway: Benchmarking Persistent Spatial Memory Across Revisits
items.description: Persistent spatial understanding is essential for embodied agents to operate reliably in environments they repeatedly encounter.
items.ai_summary: ReSpaceBench evaluates the persistent spatial memory of embodied agents across repeated room visits, revealing that existing models and agentic frameworks struggle with room association and state tracking.

items.title: RESILAGENT: A Three-Pillar Architecture for Cyber-Physical Resilience in Electrical Power and Energy Systems
items.description: Electrical Power and Energy Systems face hybrid threats that combine cyber intrusions, physical sabotage and climate-driven stress, and routinely outpace today's siloed monitoring stacks.
items.ai_summary: RESILAGENT proposes a three-pillar architecture combining agentic AI, digital twins, and blockchain to detect and recover from hybrid cyber-physical threats in electrical power systems.

items.title: LynnReal-Hand: Unlocking World Interaction with Hand Control
items.description: Interactive video world models enable exploration through text and camera controls, yet direct object interaction requires finer control.
items.ai_summary: LynnReal-Hand introduces a hand-controlled video world model that unifies fine-grained hand-object interaction modeling with efficient streaming generation for interactive environments.

items.title: Jetriever: Shifting Agent Memory Retrieval from Similarity to Utility
items.description: A useful memory need not resemble the question it helps answer. Jetriever ranks each stored memory by Jev's decision score for its usefulness to the current question, replacing similarity search with full-pool utility scoring.
items.ai_summary: Jetriever ranks stored memories by utility scoring rather than similarity, improving retrieval accuracy for agent memory systems and question-answering tasks.

items.title: Generative AI and the Crisis of Higher Education Assessments: Examining 'AI-Proofing' Strategies for College-Level Assessments
items.description: Higher education is confronting an academic-integrity challenge unlike any in its history. Students can now outsource homework, take-home assignments, and online examinations to large language models (LLMs) that complete them in seconds.
items.ai_summary: An analysis of college-level assessments across multiple disciplines evaluates how state-of-the-art large language models perform on questions purposely designed by faculty members to be AI-resistant.

items.title: Network Intrusion Detection Adaptability under Spurious Labels: A Noise-Aware Few-Shot Class-Incremental Learning Framework
items.description: Network Intrusion Detection Systems (NIDSs) must incrementally adapt to emerging attacks, even when only a limited amount of labeled network traffic is available. Consequently, Few-Shot Class-Incremental Learning (FSCIL)-based NIDSs have gained growing attention.
items.ai_summary: NAFN is a noise-aware few-shot class-incremental learning framework that identifies mislabeled data and resamples synthetic features to help network intrusion detection systems adapt to new attacks.

items.title: Event-Triggered Visual Perception for Real-Time Harvest Outcome Estimation in Mechanical Blueberry Harvesting
items.description: Mechanical blueberry harvesting requires a balance between removing ripe fruit and avoiding premature removal of unripe berries that could remain on the bush for a later harvest.
items.ai_summary: An event-triggered machine-vision system captures and analyzes crate images locally on an industrial computer to provide real-time maturity estimates of mechanically harvested blueberries.

items.title: Subprocess-Constrained Markov Decision Processes
items.description: Constrained Markov decision processes (CMDPs) typically bound expected cumulative cost from an initial state. Such a guarantee can be insufficient when a policy must remain feasible after every history it may encounter.
items.ai_summary: Subprocess-constrained Markov decision processes introduce a stronger feasibility requirement for policies, and a polynomial-time algorithm using history-dependent policies overcomes the resulting computational obstacles.

items.title: Variationally correct physics-informed operator learning for nonlinear partial differential equations
items.description: Physics-informed operator learning trains neural operators on the residual of a parametric partial differential equation (PDE) instead of labeled solution data, but its reliability depends on a variationally correct residual: one that is equivalent to the error in a norm…
items.ai_summary: Variationally correct physics-informed operator learning uses first-order system least-squares residuals to train neural operators for nonlinear partial differential equations without requiring labeled solution data.

items.title: Generative Data Augmentation Without External Data: An Empirical and Theoretical Study on Deep Networks
items.description: Generative data augmentation adds samples from generative models to a classifier's training set. Many influential studies use generators pre-trained on large external datasets, and so mix the value of synthetic data with knowledge transferred through pretraining.
items.ai_summary: Generative data augmentation without external data can improve classifier test accuracy when the real and generated distributions have a small discrepancy and the baseline classifier has room for improvement.

items.title: Warm Starting Neural Dynamics Models From Few Jacobian Samples
items.description: Model-based reinforcement learning (MBRL) leverages a model of the environment, used for planning and generating samples without interacting with the real world.
items.ai_summary: TDec-Init is an algorithm that warm-starts neural dynamics models using transition Jacobians decomposed from stacked tensor samples to improve sample efficiency in reinforcement learning.

items.title: ExRel: Learning Directed Reuse Relevance between Rich-Text K-12 Question Images with Executable Relation Contracts
items.description: In K-12 education, question images combine text, mathematical expressions, diagrams, and diverse layouts. Variations in wording, conditions, answer options, or task scope can substantially alter their reuse utility despite visual similarity.
items.ai_summary: ExRel is an agentic, code-grounded framework for synthesizing and validating educational question images to improve directed reuse relevance grading in K-12 learning tasks.

items.title: Balanced Twin Weight Factorization for Efficient MLLMs
items.description: Weight Factorization (WF) methods aim to reduce a model's latency, memory, or both. These typically decompose a pretrained model into two or more factors that approximate the original model weights with fewer parameters and floating point operations (FLOPs).
items.ai_summary: Balanced Twin Weight Factorization uses factorized model structures and balancing techniques to simultaneously lower inference latency and increase learning capacity in multimodal large language models.

items.title: A Scalable Multi Task Learning Framework for Modeling Demographic Disagreements in Annotation Tasks
items.description: Annotators from different demographic backgrounds often disagree in systematic ways due to varying lived experiences, cultural contexts, and their relationship to the content.
items.ai_summary: Stakeholder-Aware Joint Multi-Task Learning is a framework that models demographic disagreements in annotation tasks to improve group-level performance in toxicity detection without requiring privacy-invasive individual details.

items.title: Out of Sight, Into Memory: Compact Visual Latents Retain Local Evidence in Ultra-High-Resolution Remote Sensing
items.description: Question answering over ultra-high-resolution (UHR) remote sensing scenes poses a tension for multimodal large language models: global overviews obscure small objects and local attributes, whereas detailed crops consume substantial context.
items.ai_summary: Compact visual latents encode high-resolution remote sensing crops into short memory sequences, retaining fine-grained local evidence for multimodal large language models while compressing context.

items.title: Expertise capture in workplace AI
items.description: AI assistants are becoming part of how knowledge workers think and perform, accumulating the prompts, exemplars, memory and interaction histories that encode a worker's professional judgment. This infrastructure typically runs under employer or platform control.
items.ai_summary: Expertise capture is a conceptual framework describing how knowledge workers' professional judgments are absorbed into AI resources under organizational control and retained when workers depart.

items.title: Comments on "Deep Fréchet Regression"
items.description: We discuss the Journal of the American Statistical Association (JASA) discussion paper "Deep Fréchet Regression" and explore an alternative perspective based on conditional flow matching.
items.ai_summary: Conditional flow matching offers an alternative perspective to deep Fréchet regression by learning covariate-dependent transport directly within the response space for modeling full conditional distributions.

items.title: Replicating and Extending Weight-Space Programming: Frontier LLMs Compile Programs into Weights and Read Input Layers
items.description: Researchers at MIT recently reported that GPT-6 Astra, a frontier large language model (LLM), can write the weights of small neural networks directly in a single reply, and can read the raw weights of small networks to say what they were trained to do.
items.ai_summary: Evaluation study showing that frontier large language models can directly compile programs into neural network weights and read raw weights to analyze small networks.

items.title: Learning to Reason with Predictive Gains for Generative Recommendation
items.description: Reasoning-enhanced generative recommendation (GR) has attracted increasing attention for leveraging the reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLMs) to improve next-item prediction.
items.ai_summary: Training framework that optimizes reasoning in generative recommendation models using predictive gain to provide contribution-aware rewards for individual reasoning steps.

items.title: [CLS] and [EOS] Tokens are not Enough for CLIP-based Class-Incremental Learning
items.description: Class-Incremental Learning (CIL) aims to empower models to continuously acquire new knowledge while mitigating catastrophic forgetting.
items.ai_summary: Cross-modal enhancement method that leverages local visual patches and textual tokens from CLIP to improve class-incremental learning while preserving previous knowledge.

items.title: A Reinforcement Learning Method to Navigate SMEFT Operator Space
items.description: A reinforcement learning agent with a lightweight actor-critic architecture explores the Standard Model Effective Field Theory operator space to discover diverse high-quality theory hypotheses and improve global fits.
items.ai_summary: Reinforcement learning method that navigates high-dimensional particle physics parameter spaces to efficiently discover diverse, high-quality Standard Model Effective Field Theory hypotheses.

items.title: Power Line Detection in Point Clouds with Point-SAM and RANSAC
items.description: This article deals with the problem of detecting the position of power lines in airborne laser scanning point clouds. We address both the problem of segmenting power lines from background like ground and vegetation and of identifying individual lines.
items.ai_summary: Comparison of segmentation and RANSAC detection methods on airborne LiDAR point clouds to accurately isolate and identify individual power lines across varying terrain.

items.title: Variational Monte Carlo for Quantum Excited States via Nested Low-Rank Approximation
items.description: The electronic Schrödinger equation encodes a molecule's electronic structure and quantum properties, but solving it scales exponentially with the number of electrons.
items.ai_summary: Variational Monte Carlo algorithm that computes molecular quantum excited states using a low-rank approximation reparameterization to overcome exponential scaling hurdles.

items.title: Just sort it! A note on the LP behind rank-one anti-loop edits
items.description: Weight-space programming removes the thinking loops of a small reasoning model by a rank-one edit W' = W + u v^T of an MLP output matrix, where u is a loop direction and v is the solution of a sparse Linear Program (LP) over the neuron activations.
items.ai_summary: Study showing that replacing a linear program with a simple sorting strategy for weight-space programming edits maintains high performance on language math tasks.

items.title: Emergent Steering Beyond Endpoint Alignment in Chemical Reaction Models
items.description: Machine learning models for chemical reaction prediction are usually evaluated by endpoint accuracy, but endpoint correctness alone does not reveal how a model represents chemical transformation or why it fails.
items.ai_summary: Unified forward-retrosynthesis framework that uses shared latent space geometry to decompose chemical reaction model updates into endpoint-parallel and residual components for auditing.

items.title: Rubric-Based AES with LLM Ensembles: Scoring of Student Responses in Critical Online Reasoning Using Ensembles of LLMs
items.description: Grading student responses is costly and time-consuming. Moreover, human annotators are prone to bias, fatigue, and rater drift, which further limits grading reliability.
items.ai_summary: Automated essay scoring evaluation demonstrating that large language model ensembles match human-rater agreement across multiple rubric criteria for student responses.

items.title: AuXSpec: Learning to Autoformalize Program Specifications via Executable Postconditions
items.description: Formal specifications define intended program behavior and underpin verification, but writing them in theorem provers such as Lean is slow and expertise-intensive, making specification a major bottleneck to scaling formally correct code.
items.ai_summary: Lean framework that pairs declarative program specifications with executable counterparts to provide reinforcement-learning rewards and improve formal specification generation models.

items.title: Quality and Similarity Indicators for Video-Based Heart Rate and Respiratory Rate Fusion: A Controlled Evaluation
items.description: Camera-based heart rate (HR) and respiratory rate (RR) estimates vary in reliability from window to window, and a common remedy is to fuse several extraction methods with weights from reference-free signal quality indicators.
items.ai_summary: This research paper evaluates quality indicators and similarity measures for fusing camera-based heart rate and respiratory rate extraction methods, finding that quality-weighted fusion significantly reduces heart rate error.

items.title: Flexible Multi-Stack Super-Resolution of Clinical Brain MRI Using Hetero-Orientation Variational Encoding: Expert Reader Evaluation in a Nigerian Cohort
items.description: MS-HVED enables flexible super-resolution of partially overlapping brain MRI stacks by fusing independently encoded multi-scale Gaussian posteriors with a field-of-view-aware Product-of-Gaussians and physics-informed domain randomisation, improving reconstruction, tissue…
items.ai_summary: This research paper introduces MS-HVED, a sequence-agnostic framework for flexible multi-stack brain MRI super-resolution that improves reconstruction fidelity and downstream tissue segmentation across diverse clinical conditions.

items.title: Do Embedding-Map Distances Guide LLM Ideation? Four Tests Against What Came Next
items.description: A popular ideation recipe treats an embedding map of existing work as a guide: pick points far from everything and decode them into ideas. I test four ways such distances could guide ideation against what appeared later.
items.ai_summary: This paper tests four ways embedding-map distances can guide language model ideation against actual subsequent developments, revealing limitations in using far directions and density gap scores for generating new ideas.

items.title: Harness Leverage Across Model Size: A Ladder of Five Local Agent Harnesses from 0.75B to 4.7B
items.description: A harness turns a model into a system that completes tasks: it builds the prompt, exposes tools and decides when work is done. Harness comparisons hold the model fixed. Model comparisons hold the harness fixed.
items.ai_summary: This paper investigates how different local agent harnesses affect model task completion across various sizes, showing that specific harness designs significantly determine whether models successfully execute and save work.

items.title: Shaping AI's Beliefs Before It Generates: Human Sense of Agency in Creative AI
items.description: AI systems for creative media generation expand human capabilities yet risk diminishing human agency. A core problem is anchoring, where the user's thinking becomes anchored to a polished, generated artifact, shifting the user's role from active authoring to reactive editing.
items.ai_summary: This paper proposes pre-generation belief controls, instantiated in a system called PaCC, to let users inspect and steer an AI's assumptions before creative media generation, enhancing their sense of agency.

items.title: Efficient Modeling of Multi-Agent Systems via Structure-Aware Physics-Informed Learning
items.description: Modeling large multi-agent systems poses challenges for trajectory inference and parameter identification, as network size and coupling increase computational demands and partial observations require reconstructing unobserved states.
items.ai_summary: This paper proposes MAS-PINN, a physics-informed neural network architecture that leverages network topology and agent similarity to efficiently simulate and identify large multi-agent systems with reduced computational costs.

items.title: Portrait Fitness as a Pretext: Probing Implicit Demographic Bias in VLMs
items.description: We audit face-related bias in VLMs using BALPORTRAITS, a new balanced dataset of 9,000 fictional portraits across ethnicity, gender, and age segments.
items.ai_summary: This research paper introduces a balanced dataset of fictional portraits to audit face-related demographic biases in vision-language models across occupations, brands, and activities, revealing widespread statistical disparities.

items.title: MegNIST, A Benchmark for Non-Invasive Inner Speech Decoding
items.description: MegNIST is a benchmark dataset for developing and evaluating machine learning methods for inner speech decoding from magnetoencephalography (MEG).
items.ai_summary: This paper presents MegNIST, a benchmark dataset of magnetoencephalography recordings for developing and evaluating machine learning methods for non-invasive inner speech decoding.

items.title: Self-attention is a Dyson equation for many-body machine learning
items.description: Why does symmetric sum-pooling (DeepSets) predict ground-state potentials to sub-meV accuracy, yet fail for correlated wavefunctions and excited states?
items.ai_summary: This research paper proves that self-attention functions as a real-space Dyson iteration whose softmax kernel acts as a two-body self-energy capable of capturing correlations in physical systems.

items.title: Beyond Bilingual: Studying Quadrilingual Code-Switching with Conversational AI
items.description: Multilingual speakers choose languages by topic and conversation partner. Large language models (LLMs) support these languages unequally. Research on code-switching with conversational AI has mostly examined bilingual pairs of well-resourced languages.
items.ai_summary: This study examines quadrilingual code-switching among multilingual speakers conversing with chatbots in Curaçao and Aruba, highlighting the need for conversational AI to better handle turn-by-turn language changes and low-resource languages.

items.title: Train After You Measure: a Pre-Registered Learning Curve for Fine-Tuning Typed Decision Models on One User's Labels
items.description: Fine-tuning a small typed decision model on one user's email labels did not clear the margin we pre-registered over a logistic regression trained on the same labels.
items.ai_summary: Study analyzing fine-tuned small decision models on user email labels finds that performance remains close to or below simple logistic regression baselines.

items.title: VideoNexus: Video Perception Beyond the Reasoning Context
items.description: VideoNexus separates detailed video perception from evidence-driven planning and reasoning, using perception sub-agents to return compact temporally grounded evidence and achieving higher accuracy at lower cost on long-video benchmarks.
items.ai_summary: VideoNexus is a training-free framework that separates detailed video perception from reasoning, achieving high accuracy on long video understanding benchmarks at reduced API costs.

items.title: Nonparametric Instrumental Kernel Regression: The Well- and Misspecified Setting Under General Link Conditions
items.description: We study nonparametric instrumental variable regression when the outcome takes values in a separable Hilbert space $\mathbb{Y}$, for instance a curve, a density or the kernel mean embedding of a distribution.
items.ai_summary: Nonparametric instrumental kernel regression method extends kernel instrumental variable regression to Hilbert-space-valued outcomes using two-stage spectral regularisation and non-asymptotic bounds.

items.title: Stability-Compensated Threshold Calibration for Selection-Conditioned Risk Control in Large Language Models
items.description: Large language models often produce hallucinated answers, motivating selective prediction policies that abstain on uncertain queries. However, heuristic uncertainty thresholds alone do not provide statistical control of errors among accepted predictions.
items.ai_summary: Stability-Compensated Linear Expectation Control is a calibration method for large language models that prevents threshold-selection instability and ensures finite-sample error rate control.

items.title: The Mask Is Not the Object: Volumetric Supervision for 3D Gaussian Segmentation
items.description: A plug-and-play objective, VODA, groups per-pixel contributors by local depth to supervise all Gaussians in selected depth clusters, improving volumetric segmentation and enabling evaluation via Removal-3D and Removal Depth Error.
items.ai_summary: VODA is a volumetric supervision objective that uses local depth structure to improve 3D Gaussian segmentation by directly supervising all Gaussians in selected depth clusters.

items.title: VisualArtifactSpec 1.0: Evaluating Visual Artifacts under Task Specifications
items.description: Visual artifact tasks test agents' ability to translate task specifications and source materials into outputs that meet practical needs. Evaluation across artifact families helps distinguish broadly applicable authoring capabilities from strengths confined to a particular medium.
items.ai_summary: VisualArtifactSpec 1.0 is a benchmark of 211 creation and modification tasks designed to evaluate visual artifacts across presentations, graphics, animations, and web interfaces.

items.title: A Crowd-Audited Atlas of Implicit Bias in LLM-Powered Agents
items.description: Prior work has shown that large language models (LLMs) express implicit biases in high-publicity, one-off decision scenarios such as hiring and intelligence assessment.
items.ai_summary: Atlas of 506 decision scenarios from time-use data demonstrates significant implicit bias in LLM-powered agents across multiple daily activity domains.

items.title: Proceedings Eighth International Workshop on Formal Methods for Autonomous Systems
items.description: This EPTCS volume contains the papers from the Eighth International Workshop on Formal Methods for Autonomous Systems (FMAS 2026), which was held on the 17th and 18th of November 2026.

items.title: WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent for Omni AI-Generated Video Detection
items.description: WeVisForensics coordinates self-evolving visual and audio forensic inspector agents under a dual-timescale reinforcement learning policy to detect generated-video artifacts with localized evidence and high accuracy.
items.ai_summary: WeVisForensics is an agentic framework that uses dual-timescale policy optimization to coordinate forensic inspectors and accurately detect AI-generated videos across various benchmarks.

items.title: Learning What Pairs Miss for Higher-Order Multimodal Alignment
items.description: Contrastive learning beyond two modalities now scores the whole tuple with multilinear products, volumes, and fusion heads, critics that can represent the joint distribution. In practice these critics still behave like bags of pairs.
items.ai_summary: CHORD is a contrastive learning method that uses calibrated pairwise decoys to train higher-order multimodal alignment models on samples requiring multiple modalities.

items.title: Federated TD Learning in Heterogeneous Environments with Average Rewards: A Two-timescale Approach with Polyak-Ruppert Averaging
items.description: Federated Reinforcement Learning (FRL) provides a promising way to speedup training in reinforcement learning when one has access to multiple edge devices that can operate in parallel.
items.ai_summary: This paper proposes a two-timescale federated reinforcement learning method with iterate averaging that achieves optimal convergence and linear speedup for heterogeneous environments with average rewards.

items.title: Premise Recovery in Software Design: What Does This Decision Rest On?
items.description: Design decisions shape software architecture, and writing them down preserves the reasons behind it. Architecture decision records (ADRs) capture them, each with its context, choice, and consequences.
items.ai_summary: This paper investigates premise recovery in software design by evaluating open-weight language models on finding unnamed architectural decision records that earlier decisions rest upon.

items.title: ALIVE: Making Streaming Video Models Interactive
items.description: Streaming video LLMs can continuously observe the world, yet often handle user requests in isolation. We introduce ALIVE, an interactive streaming video model supporting proactive monitoring, streaming task coordination, and feedback-seeking interaction.
items.ai_summary: This paper introduces ALIVE, an interactive streaming video model that uses contrastive supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning to support proactive monitoring, task coordination, and feedback-seeking interactions.

items.title: Exploring the link between predictive uncertainty and the sim-to-real gap in deep learning models utilizing synthetic data
items.description: Today, state-of-the-art methods for quality control (QC) are based on Machine Vision, combining deep learning (DL) models with camera-based inspection.
items.ai_summary: This study uses an ensemble method to demonstrate that predictive uncertainty in deep learning models increases under sim-to-real domain shifts when utilizing synthetic data for quality control.

items.title: Symmetry Detection with Patch Embedding Models by Means of a Scalar Product Transform
items.description: We present a transformation of vector embeddings representing image patches into scores for point reflection symmetry at the crossing points of patches.
items.ai_summary: This paper introduces the Scalar Product Transform, which converts pre-trained patch embedding models into point reflection symmetry scores and bounding boxes without requiring specialized training.

items.title: What You Post Is What You Symptom: Estimating Psychometric Networks from Social Media Discourse
items.description: Symptom networks in psychopathology are estimated almost exclusively from self-report questionnaires, restricting inference to whatever symptom set a given instrument covers.
items.ai_summary: This paper presents a framework for estimating symptom-resolved psychometric networks directly from social media discourse to study conditions like depression and eating disorders.

items.title: Specificity-Guided Knowledge Diversion for Decomposable Generative Models
items.description: Generative model pre-training typically optimizes a model as a whole without explicitly organizing its parameters for selective reuse. Decomposable pre-training instead learns reusable components for downstream adaptation while retaining strong generative performance.
items.ai_summary: This paper proposes Specificity-Guided Knowledge Diversion, a method that learns how generative knowledge is shared and specialized using Knowledge Units to improve both generation and downstream reuse.

items.title: Representational Change Under Self-Consuming Training: A Sparse Autoencoder Analysis
items.description: Large language models are increasingly exposed to model-generated text, raising the possibility that future models will be trained recursively on the outputs of their predecessors.
items.ai_summary: This study analyzes how internal representations and sparse autoencoders evolve across five generations of recursive training on model-generated text.

items.title: TEMPO: Regime-Aware Operator Learning with Locally Adapted POD Bases
items.description: Operator learning approximates the solution map of a parametric partial differential equation from data, enabling fast prediction at new parameter values without repeated simulation.
items.ai_summary: This paper proposes TEMPO, a regime-aware operator learning framework using locally adapted proper orthogonal decomposition bases and a mixture of operators to predict parametric partial differential equation solutions.

items.title: MovieRoll: A Systematic Framework for Rolling Out Long-Form Videos
items.description: Streaming video generation must sustain quality beyond the training horizon while handling self-generated history and growing cache costs.

items.title: Anchoring Motion, Refining Trajectories: Generalizable Continuous Neural Decoding
items.description: Brain activity encodes motor information across multiple temporal scales, enabling continuous neural control beyond discrete action recognition.
items.ai_summary: This paper introduces AMRT, a shared neural decoding framework that uses a two-stage anchor-and-refine design to achieve generalizable continuous neural control across heterogeneous subjects and movement paradigms.

items.title: TRIAGE-CPG: A Cross-Model Study of Budgeted Static Malware Triage with Large Language Models
items.description: When triaging unknown binaries, security analysts must decide which samples to clear as benign, flag as malicious, or escalate for deeper analysis.
items.ai_summary: TRIAGE-CPG is a fixed pipeline that uses Large Language Models to select and analyze functions in decompiled binaries for budgeted static malware triage.

items.title: Wavelet-Energy-Driven Dynamic Patching for Time Series Forecasting
items.description: Patch-based transformers tokenise a time series into fixed-size, uniform windows, which commits the model to a single temporal resolution even though real signals are multi-scale.
items.ai_summary: A wavelet-energy-driven dynamic patching method for time series forecasting transforms multi-scale signal decompositions into variable-length patches to improve prediction accuracy without learnable filters.

items.title: Benchleaking Is Accelerating: Benchmark contamination has worsened sharply in the past month -- from post-training down to pre-training base models
items.description: Benchmark contamination is not new, but recent model releases show it in a sharper form. We use the term benchleaking for the case in which a benchmark's own test examples enter training data, so that a score reflects recall rather than capability.
items.ai_summary: An analysis of benchmark contamination reveals that test examples increasingly leak into pre-training and post-training data, inflating model scores through recall rather than genuine capability.

items.title: A2A-UAV: A Multimodal Air-to-Air Dataset for UAV Detection and Identification
items.description: The rapid growth of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) in low-altitude airspace increases the risk of unauthorized intrusions, making reliable detection and identification of non-cooperative UAVs essential for low-altitude airspace safety.
items.ai_summary: A2A-UAV is a multimodal air-to-air dataset containing over 100,000 time-aligned samples of RGB, panoramic, thermal, RF, and radar data for detecting and identifying unmanned aerial vehicles.

items.title: Can AI Mature a Model's Geometry? Training-Free Weight Baking in LLMs
items.description: Can an AI make a trained language model more mature, in the sense of a better organized latent space, by looking only at the geometry of that space?
items.ai_summary: A training-free method uses topological descriptors and closed-form ridge regression to reorganize the latent space geometry of language models without altering raw weights.

items.title: Rotation-Invariant Machine Learning for Highly Symmetric Molecular Configurations
items.description: Atomistic machine learning can approximate expensive quantum mechanical calculations at a fraction of their computational cost, but accuracy depends strongly on how the three-dimensional atomic environments are represented.
items.ai_summary: An extended invariant basis for HIP-HOP resolves symmetry degeneracies in atomic representations, achieving high accuracy and faster inference for molecular configurations.

items.title: Programmable Semantic Interventions: Learning Causal Carriers from Behavioral Programs
items.description: Causal abstraction explains a frozen network by aligning its activations with the variables of a simpler, interpretable model, and checking that interventions on the two agree.
items.ai_summary: Programmable Semantic Interventions is a method that uses user-defined semantic programs to learn low-rank activation subspaces for interpreting neural networks without requiring ground-truth labels.

items.title: Share your Screen and Talk to Gemini: How Young Learners Interact with Multimodal GenAI While Solving Scratch Tasks
items.description: Children using Scratch to learn programming can struggle with text-heavy, lengthy explanations and hints during debugging. Verbal interactions based on screen sharing or camera data may be an interesting alternative for supporting learners.
items.ai_summary: A multimodal GenAI voice tutor for fifth- and sixth-graders learning Scratch programming provides actionable debugging hints, though it frequently misses code errors while students overly trust its answers.

items.title: High-probability Uniform Mixing via Dobrushin Contraction and Accelerated Hamiltonian Monte Carlo
items.description: Hamiltonian Monte Carlo, since its invention and subsequent rise to widespread use, has been motivated by its ability to accelerate convergence to equilibrium compared to diffusive methods, both in terms of dependence on condition number and dimension.
items.ai_summary: An accelerated Hamiltonian Monte Carlo algorithm achieves faster convergence to equilibrium for strongly convex targets by combining coupling technology with Dobrushin contraction.

items.title: Fix, Don't Retake: Physics-Simulated Training for Correcting Patient Positioning Errors in Dental Panoramic Radiographs
items.description: Patient-positioning errors can distort panoramic radiographs and lead to repeat examinations. This study investigated artificial intelligence for correcting these errors in existing images.
items.ai_summary: A physics-simulated training approach uses generated pairs of dental radiographs to correct patient-positioning errors and improve image quality in existing scans.

items.title: Syllable- and Word-Level Evaluation of Tibetan OCR
items.description: Optical character recognition (OCR) for Tibetan is evaluated predominantly by character error rate (CER). Tibetan marks syllable boundaries but does not mark word boundaries, so a word error rate requires a segmenter.
items.ai_summary: Study evaluates nine Tibetan optical character recognition configurations across syllable- and word-level error rates to establish baseline benchmarks for script styles.

items.title: Déjà-Events: Multi-view 3D Geometry with Event Cameras via Sparsity-Aware Adaptive Gating
items.description: Event cameras keep capturing structure where conventional cameras blur or saturate, which makes them attractive for 3D perception in fast or poorly lit scenes.
items.ai_summary: Event-only model called Déjà-Events predicts depth, camera pose, and pointmaps from multiple views in a single forward pass using sparsity-aware adaptive gating.

items.title: Latent Bridge: Asking for Help Without Words
items.description: Text-based model collaboration requires a large model to generate intermediate responses before a smaller model can use its guidance, adding large-model decoding cost to inference.
items.ai_summary: Method called POND uses a frozen large sender model for prefill and a small receiver model for decoding to improve small-model generation without large-model decoding costs.

items.title: LATTE-WordSeg-Lite: Multi-Granularity Thai Word Segmentation on a CPU, with a Reproducible Benchmark
items.description: Large language models read Thai through subword tokens, without a word segmenter. Yet Thai treebanks, speech metrics and morphological resources are built on words, often at several granularities, and word boundaries resolve ambiguities that subword tokens leave open.
items.ai_summary: Distilled CPU segmenter called LATTE-WordSeg-Lite outputs compounds, words, and morphemes in one pass while running significantly faster than existing models.

items.title: Turing Agent: Agentic Formal Verification for Mathematical Research
items.description: Large language models (LLMs) are rapidly advancing mathematical discovery, moving beyond benchmark-level problem solving to tackle frontier research problems.
items.ai_summary: Agent harness called Turing Agent integrates theorem and proof formalization agents to orchestrate end-to-end formal verification of research-level mathematics.

items.title: Agent-Native by Design: A Programming Language for Agentic Applications
items.description: Building agentic applications requires combining large language model (LLM) operations, workflow structure and application state, and model-guided routing.
items.ai_summary: Programming language called Jac unifies model operations, workflow structure, and model-guided routing to reduce AI-integration code and simplify agent development.

items.title: Deep Learning for Physicists: From Linear Regression to Reasoning Models
items.description: These lecture notes are based on an introductory course on neural networks and deep learning that the author taught in the School of Mathematical Sciences at Queen Mary University of London in 2023/24 and 2024/25.
items.ai_summary: Lecture notes provide a self-contained introductory guide to neural networks, deep learning, and large language models using physical intuition rather than heavy formalism.

items.title: AnachroBench: Evaluating Historical Consistency in Large Vision-Language Models
items.description: Existing Large Vision-Language Model benchmarks primarily evaluate visual understanding in general everyday scenarios, leaving historical consistency with a specified era and country largely underexplored.
items.ai_summary: Controlled benchmark called AnachroBench evaluates historical consistency in visual scenes by testing large vision-language models on image pairs containing seamlessly inserted modern objects.

items.title: Benchmarking Large Language Models for Linguistic Annotation
items.description: Assessing large language models for linguistic annotation requires task-specific evaluation under documented conditions. We present dhAIBench, a Python benchmarking and annotation tool with a web interface for exploring and sharing results.
items.ai_summary: Python benchmarking tool called dhAIBench records prompts and predictions to evaluate large language models across multiple linguistic annotation tasks.

items.title: FM-Recon: Exploring Foundation Model Features for Accelerated Cardiac Cine MRI Reconstruction
items.description: Foundation models have demonstrated strong feature extraction capabilities across various medical imaging tasks, yet their potential for MRI reconstruction remains largely unexplored, particularly within unrolled reconstruction networks and under artifact-corrupted inputs.
items.ai_summary: Framework called FM-Recon integrates features from pretrained foundation models into unrolled reconstruction networks to accelerate cardiac cine MRI reconstruction.

items.title: Compressed Simulation-Based Inference: Neural Posterior Estimation for Massive Data via Low-Dimensional Sketches
items.description: Neural posterior estimation (NPE) is a popular Bayesian simulation-based inference (SBI) approach that uses neural networks trained on simulated data--parameter pairs to approximate the posterior given a user-chosen prior.
items.ai_summary: Neural posterior estimation method that uses low-dimensional data sketches to match embedding network performance while increasing computational efficiency for massive data.

items.title: The Price of Not Planning: Parallel Sampling Depth Peaks at the Reconstruction Threshold
items.description: Masked diffusion models sample the tokens of one round independently. Planned decoders first generate a coarse plan, then fill in the tokens in parallel. We ask when a plan saves rounds, how many it saves, and how fine it must be.
items.ai_summary: Analysis of masked diffusion models showing that planned decoders save rounds most effectively near the reconstruction threshold when using small planning units.

items.title: PLECTA: Overlap-aware instance segmentation of dense strand networks from binary masks
items.description: Many materials and tissues, including carbon-nanotube sheets, collagen and paper, comprise overlapping strands whose arrangement influences their effective properties.
items.ai_summary: Deterministic segmentation method that traces individual overlapping strands from binary images by formulating junction decisions as maximum-weight partial-matching problems.

items.title: Classical structural priors improve neural molecular representations in molecule language models
items.description: Classical molecular similarity is central to chemical information systems, yet molecule-language models trained on paired structure-text data do not necessarily organize molecular embeddings according to graded structural relationships.
items.ai_summary: Training-only regularizer that aligns molecular language model representations with Tanimoto similarity to improve structure-based retrieval and property prediction.

items.title: CAE-Bench: Benchmarking AI Agents for Reusable CAE Solver Development
items.description: We developed CAE-Bench, a benchmark to evaluate AI agents on Computer-Aided Engineering (CAE) solver development.
items.ai_summary: Benchmark to evaluate the ability of AI agents to develop reusable Computer-Aided Engineering solvers that generalize to unseen inputs.

items.title: In-Context Estimation and Prediction for Parametric ODEs
items.description: Transformers have demonstrated the ability to perform in-context learning, that is, to adapt to new tasks from a few examples without updating their parameters.
items.ai_summary: Framework using transformers to perform parameter estimation and trajectory prediction for parametric ordinary differential equations via approximate maximum likelihood.

items.title: Conformal Expert Pools: Training-Free Probabilistic Time-Series Forecasting Beyond Seasonality
items.description: Conformal Seasonal Pools (CSP) showed that a forecaster with no training at all, built only from past values at the same point in the season and from past forecast errors, significantly outperformed DeepNPTS, Amazon's learned non-parametric forecaster.
items.ai_summary: Training-free probabilistic time-series forecasting method that builds predictive distributions from a pool of simple forecasters and their past errors.

items.title: Variance-adaptive confidence regions for fixed-benchmark binomial mixtures, with application to LLM evaluation
items.description: We construct confidence intervals for linear functionals $θ(F_m)=\int h\,dF_m$ of the empirical law $F_m$ of success probabilities $p_1,\dots,p_m$, from independent counts $c_i\sim\mathrm{Bin}(n,p_i)$, as for a language model run $n$ times per problem.
items.ai_summary: Method for constructing variance-adaptive confidence intervals for binomial mixtures to evaluate language models across various rollouts and bounded functionals.

items.title: Leveraging Binary Hashing for Scalable Index Assignment in Semantic Communications
items.description: Transmitting semantically structured embedding vectors over digital channels is costly in bit rate, while conven- tional vector quantization approaches face limitations in scalabil- ity, encoding complexity, and index assignment.
items.ai_summary: Semantic communication approach using binary hashing and iterative quantization to compress and transmit embeddings efficiently over digital channels.

items.title: Dimension-free spectral laws and the risk of spectral filters
items.description: Spectral properties of the sample covariance are key to modern machine learning with high-dimensional data. Random matrix theory (RMT) supplies powerful tools; however, most classical results assume proportional asymptotics, where $d/n$ tends to a finite limit.
items.ai_summary: Dimension-free spectral theory for high-dimensional data in Hilbert spaces that establishes deterministic equivalents and nonasymptotic error bounds for sample covariance.

items.title: QuantileGS: Quantile-Based Conformal Bounds on RGB Rendering Errors for Novel View Synthesis with 3D Gaussian Splatting
items.description: Uncertainty quantification for novel view synthesis with 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) assesses rendering reliability at unseen viewpoints. This reliability depends on the discrepancy between rendered and true colors, which cannot be measured without ground-truth images.
items.ai_summary: QuantileGS is a post-hoc framework combining learned rendering-error quantiles with scale-normalized conformal calibration to produce spatially adaptive error bounds for 3D Gaussian Splatting novel view synthesis.

items.title: The Price of Choosing Examples: Context Overfitting in Adaptive In-Context Learning
items.description: In-context learning is usually analyzed as if the examples in the prompt were sampled before the learner is chosen. In deployed systems they are not: examples are retrieved, filtered, re-ranked, edited, and repeatedly tested after seeing the query and the data store.
items.ai_summary: Context generalization bounds and PAC-Bayesian retrieval rules are proposed to formalize prompt construction as adaptive data analysis and quantify context capacity in in-context learning.

items.title: Stream of Belief: Eliciting Collective Intelligence through Latent Belief Dynamics
items.description: In this work, we view multi-agent reasoning as a process of seeking a collective equilibrium of implicit belief dynamics and introduce Stream of Belief (SoB), where agents maintain continuous latent beliefs and iteratively refine them through communication and reflection.
items.ai_summary: Stream of Belief is a multi-agent reasoning method that enables agents to maintain continuous latent beliefs and iteratively refine them through communication and reflection.

items.title: Heteroscedastic Gaussian Process Q-learning for Sample Efficient Experimentation
items.description: Self-driving laboratories must learn to control a process from tens to hundreds of expensive experiments, too few for deep reinforcement learning (RL).
items.ai_summary: Heteroscedastic Gaussian Process Q-learning models the Q-function directly using a Gaussian process with heteroscedastic noise variance to achieve sample-efficient experimentation in self-driving laboratories.

items.title: Anytime-Valid PAC-Bayes Certificates for Adaptive Test-Time Scaling
items.description: Test-time scaling systems often choose how much to sample, which prompt to use, and which verifier or aggregation rule to trust after repeatedly inspecting a calibration set. Standard validation error bars are not valid after this adaptive selection.
items.ai_summary: Time-uniform PAC-Bayes certificates are proved for test-time scaling systems to provide valid risk bounds that hold simultaneously over all calibration times and adaptive recipe selections.

items.title: How Developer Personality Shapes the Use of AI Coding Assistants
items.description: Developers differ in personality traits that shape how they approach software development tasks, yet AI coding assistants either behave uniformly or offer personalization features whose fit with individual developers must be found through trial and error.
items.ai_summary: An exploratory survey of developers provides initial empirical evidence connecting Big Five personality traits to their perceptions and experiences with AI coding assistants.

items.title: Language-model agents' beliefs can be manipulated via truthful evidence in open channel
items.description: Language-model agents' beliefs can be manipulated through open channels such as social media, even when the information they receive is truthful.
items.ai_summary: Generative Montage coordinates language-model agents to arrange truthful information into misleading narratives, demonstrating how truthful evidence in open channels can manipulate agent beliefs.

items.title: A Study on Performance Enhancement of a Webcam-Based Real-Time Eye-Tracking System
items.description: This study proposes a real-time gaze-tracking system that uses a standard RGB webcam to estimate screen coordinates. The system combines ETH-XGaze-based gaze estimation with nine-point calibration and polynomial ridge regression.
items.ai_summary: A real-time gaze-tracking system combines ETH-XGaze-based estimation, nine-point calibration, polynomial ridge regression, and conditional pose correction to estimate screen coordinates using a standard RGB webcam.

items.title: A Generative AI-Driven Architecture for Whole-Home Intelligent Services: Edge Models, Memory Management, and Household Applications
items.description: Generative artificial intelligence is entering the home.
items.ai_summary: A design-oriented review framework maps generative artificial intelligence architectures for whole-home intelligent services using a home local server as the unifying organizing axis.

items.title: Investigating the Benefit of Transfer Learning from the Locus Coeruleus for Substantia Nigra Pars Compacta Segmentation
items.description: The substantia nigra pars compacta (SNpc) is a small midbrain nucleus that degenerates early in Parkinson's disease (PD). T1-weighted FLASH MRI enables its visualization and may support early detection of neurodegeneration.
items.ai_summary: A study evaluating transfer learning from the locus coeruleus to a 3D U-Net model finds that initialization from the locus coeruleus offers no significant benefit for segmenting the substantia nigra pars compacta.

items.title: Oriented Semi-DETR for Semi-Supervised Aerial Object Detection
items.description: Semi-supervised object detection has recently been extended to DETR, where oriented boxes introduce an ambiguity that does not arise for axis-aligned boxes: the map from parameters to rectangles is two-to-one, since $(c_x,c_y,w,h,θ)$ and $(c_x,c_y,h,w,θ+π/2)$ denote the same…
items.ai_summary: Oriented Semi-DETR is a parameter-free semi-supervised aerial object detection framework that resolves geometric ambiguity in oriented bounding boxes to outperform existing baselines.

items.title: boringmarketer/boring-marketing-skills
items.description: 31 free marketing skills for your AI agent: research, positioning, copy, pages, SEO, AI search, ads, email and content, plus a deep local-business pack. MIT.
items.ai_summary: A collection of free marketing skills helps AI agents perform tasks such as audience research, brand positioning, and content creation.

items.title: Verifiable Random Sampling of Private Data Without a Trusted Single Party
items.description: Problem: When a party supports claims about a private dataset by disclosing a sample, auditors cannot tell whether it was drawn at random or "cherry-picked" to hide flaws in the rest of the data.
items.ai_summary: NoCherry is a verifiable random sampling protocol that uses decentralized randomness beacons and cryptographic commitments to allow auditors to check private datasets without exposing them.

items.title: InclusionMed: Benchmarking AI for Inclusive Healthcare
items.description: InclusionMed is an open medical AI evaluation initiative that audits and reproduces benchmarks across healthcare roles and capabilities, revealing that model rankings and inference costs vary by context and motivating broader, context-specific evaluation.
items.ai_summary: InclusionMed is an open medical AI evaluation initiative and benchmark suite that assesses frontier large language models across diverse healthcare roles and capabilities.

items.title: MiSTiQ: MicroScaling Trellis Quantization for Extreme KV Cache Compression
items.description: Modern large language models (LLMs) increasingly support longer contexts and serve more concurrent requests, increasing both sequence lengths and batch sizes. Both trends increase KV-cache size and memory traffic during inference.
items.ai_summary: MiSTiQ combines trellis-coded storage with microscaling formats to compress LLM KV caches to extreme low bit widths while supporting efficient low-precision computation.

items.title: Open-fMIND: A Large-Scale Open-Access fMRI Corpus for Pretraining Brain Foundation Models
items.description: Self-supervised pretraining has transformed language and vision, but its application to functional MRI (fMRI) is constrained by data access.
