items.ai_summary: IBMARL is a cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning framework that uses imitation policies and centralized critics to accelerate learning and surpass demonstrator performance.

items.title: Elliptic Sampling: Optimal Interpolant Schedules for Gaussians and Beyond
items.description: Generative modeling based on stochastic interpolants requires specifying two key choices: an interpolant schedule bridging the initial and target distributions, and an efficient discretization of the resulting probability-flow ODE.
items.ai_summary: Elliptic Sampling is a framework based on complexified ODE trajectories that provides optimal interpolant schedules and a new sampling algorithm called Zoloflow for generative models.

items.title: Why Finite Intelligence Works in an Infinite World: A Mathematical Theory
items.description: An information system often has to learn before it knows what it will be asked. A finite representation can succeed without recording an infinite environment in full when those asks share collective structure, rather than demand unrelated facts scattered arbitrarily across it.
items.ai_summary: This paper establishes a mathematical theory formalizing future-task information and finite representation bounds to explain how information systems succeed in an infinite world.

items.title: ModHarness-RL: Recasting Harnesses as Learnable and Evolving Programs for Agentic RL
items.description: Agentic reinforcement learning (RL) increasingly relies on a harness, the scaffold around the model that decides what it sees of its own interaction and what guidance it receives. Most existing approaches train under a hand-written harness that stays fixed throughout.
items.ai_summary: ModHarness-RL is a framework that treats reinforcement learning harnesses as learnable and evolving programs to improve model performance across various tasks.

items.title: Alignment by Socialization: Learning Tradeoffs Under Selection
items.description: Artificial intelligence (AI) agents are expected to complete tasks while following rules of conduct, but these objectives can conflict.
items.ai_summary: This paper studies how evolutionary selection and socialization shape an agent's tradeoffs between completing tasks and following rules of conduct.

items.title: Understanding Contextual Bias in Agricultural CNNs Through Hidden-Neuron Concept Induction
items.description: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) can classify images using background-dominated patches that contain little or none of the target object, showing that they exploit contextual information.
items.ai_summary: This research uses concept induction and quantitative image descriptors to reveal interpretable visual properties associated with hidden-neuron activations in agricultural CNNs.

items.title: WaferTetris: Efficient Freeform Mapping on Wafer-Scale Accelerators
items.description: Wafer-scale accelerators offer massive compute capacity through hundreds of thousands of processing elements (PEs) interconnected across a single wafer, but realizing this potential requires efficient application mapping.
items.ai_summary: WaferTetris is a freeform mapping system for wafer-scale accelerators that flexibly packs computation to improve resource utilization and system throughput.

items.title: EventSpikeSeg: Memory-Aware Mixed-Signal Architecture for Event-Camera Spiking Segmentation
items.description: Event-camera segmentation requires persistent neural state despite sparse input events, making memory organization a central constraint on embedded implementation.
items.ai_summary: EventSpikeSeg is a mixed-signal spiking architecture that uses resident capacitor memory and shared analog processing to perform event-camera segmentation on embedded systems.

items.title: Box-conditional Hypothesis Testing for Out-of-Distribution Object Detection
items.description: Detecting out-of-distribution (OOD) objects is essential for ensuring the reliability and safety of object detectors in real-world deployment.
items.ai_summary: PLUM is a training-free score for out-of-distribution object detection that ranks a box's backbone features against in-distribution classes of the same size and border contact.

items.title: StreamEmbed: Real-Time Indexing from Pixels for Screenshot Retrieval
items.description: Screen history can serve as searchable visual memory for people and agents, but unlike an offline corpus, it must be encoded and indexed as each screenshot arrives. OCR-based indexing is fast but loses visual information; visual encoding takes over two seconds.
items.ai_summary: StreamEmbed is an incremental visual embedding system that uses spatial token pruning and temporal KV reuse to enable real-time screenshot indexing and retrieval.

items.title: Can Mechanistic Interpretability Help Explain LLM Agent Failures? A Case Study on Web Element Hallucination
items.description: Mechanistic Interpretability (MI) has made significant progress in explaining the internal computations of Large Language Models (LLMs); however, these advances have yet to demonstrate comparable success in explaining the decision-making processes of LLM-based agents.
items.ai_summary: This paper investigates why mechanistic interpretability tools struggle to fully explain web element hallucinations in LLM-based agents.

items.title: MeReader: An Offline, Privacy-Preserving, Progress-Aware AI Assistant for Narrative eBook Reading
items.description: This paper introduces MeReader, a privacy-preserving, offline and progress-aware AI assistant designed to function as a contextual companion for narrative reading on consumer hardware.
items.ai_summary: MeReader is an offline, privacy-preserving AI assistant that restricts retrieval and generation to the reader's current progress in a narrative eBook to prevent spoilers.

items.title: On numerical issues of divergences between nearly equal distributions
items.description: Barron et al. (2026) recently identified numerical issues in the softmax and soft cross-entropy loss. We show that similar issues are present in standard divergence operations between categorical distributions.
items.ai_summary: This paper identifies numerical issues in standard categorical divergence operations when distributions are nearly equal, and proposes stable reformulations.

items.title: Asymptotic Margins and Feature Confinement in Conic Classification Heads under Softmax Cross-Entropy
items.description: Classification heads built on conic functions give each class a bounded region of the feature space, and such regions are used to reject samples of unseen classes. We ask whether these regions also keep the features bounded when the head is trained with softmax cross-entropy.
items.ai_summary: This paper demonstrates that conic classification heads trained with softmax cross-entropy feature bounded class regions while maintaining positive asymptotic margins that prevent feature confinement.

items.title: Agentic induction of common data elements and information extraction from sarcoma case report abstracts
items.description: Common data elements (CDEs) support clinical data comparability but are usually defined manually. We investigated whether large language model agents could derive a CDE schema from sarcoma case report abstracts and apply it at scale.
items.ai_summary: This paper evaluates an agentic workflow that derives a common data element schema from sarcoma abstracts and extracts clinical data at scale.

items.title: Agentic AI for Discovering Fault-Tolerant Quantum Circuits
items.description: Scaling quantum computing toward practical quantum advantage is currently limited by the efficiency of circuits that operate on information encoded by quantum error-correcting codes.
items.ai_summary: Agentic AI framework uses a large language model and circuit verifier to synthesize fault-tolerant quantum error-correcting circuits through evolutionary program synthesis.

items.title: ARCHER: From Rationale Imitation to Executable Reasoning in Small Language Models
items.description: Small language models are attractive for local, low-cost, and privacy-sensitive deployment, but they remain unreliable on mathematical reasoning tasks that require decomposition, exact computation, tool use, and verification.
items.ai_summary: ARCHER is a two-stage training framework that teaches small language models to solve mathematical problems using executable action traces and calculator grounding.

items.title: TradeGauntlet: Evaluating Compliance Controls for Autonomous Trading Agents
items.description: Autonomous trading agents need controls that prevent problematic orders without making legitimate tasks impractical. We study this aspect of agentic compliance with TradeGauntlet, a replayable limit-order-book simulator that separates detection, prevention, and execution cost.
items.ai_summary: TradeGauntlet is a replayable limit-order-book simulator that evaluates compliance controls for autonomous trading agents by separating detection, prevention, and execution costs.

items.title: Interactive Program Induction with Language Model Priors
items.description: Program induction refers to the process in which a learner aims to recover a program from a few given input-output examples.
items.ai_summary: Interactive Program Induction with Language Model Priors introduces a greedy query-selection algorithm that uses a language model as a prior to recover target programs from few input-output examples.

items.title: From AI-Enabled Remote Patient Monitoring Toward Agentic Robotics: Embodiment, Governance, and Care Integration
items.description: AI-enabled remote patient monitoring is evolving beyond passive data collection toward agentic AI systems that interpret patient states, coordinate care, and initiate action across domestic and clinical settings.
items.ai_summary: Agentic robotics is proposed as a future direction for supervised systems in remote patient monitoring, connecting AI agents and robots with clinicians and patients through auditable workflows.

items.title: MMFlash: Faster Speculative Decoding for Vision-Language Models
items.description: MMFlash improves multimodal speculative decoding by adaptively upweighting visually dependent tokens and using sparse attention for long video, yielding up to 3.58× lossless speedup.

items.title: Bregman geometry in regular exponential families: dual representations and relative smoothness
items.description: Regular exponential-family distributions are ubiquitous in statistics due to their appealing and convenient properties. Notably, they can be expressed in terms of Bregman divergences, revealing fundamental connections between statistics, convex analysis, and information geometry.
items.ai_summary: Bregman geometry in regular exponential families establishes dual Bregman representations and normalization results, providing geometric characterizations of parameter spaces and relative smoothness.

items.title: Evaluating Feedback-Driven Black-Box Processes via Stochastic Modeling and Simulation
items.description: We study feedback-driven black-box processes across software engineering and machine learning. These processes are inherently sequential: policies generate inputs, observe outputs/feedback from systems, and use the feedback to guide the design of subsequent inputs.
items.ai_summary: A stochastic framework models and evaluates feedback-driven black-box processes using Markov chains and simulation to provide sound estimators and performance measures for fuzzers.

items.title: Do Verifier Judgments Survive Abstraction? Measuring Verification Transport for LLM Agent Evaluation
items.description: LLM-based verifiers are increasingly used to evaluate agent executions, but their reliability is typically measured under a single representation of the trajectory.
items.ai_summary: Verification Transport is a reliability test measuring whether LLM-based verifier judgments remain stable when execution observability changes due to abstraction-induced boundaries.

items.title: Contrastive latent representation learning with denoising score matching
items.description: Contrastive representation learning methods operate by pulling different views of the same data sample together while pushing them away from views of different samples.
items.ai_summary: ScoreCLR is a contrastive representation learning method that estimates repulsive force using denoising score matching with a lightweight network trained jointly with the encoder.

items.title: Score-based neural ordinary differential equations for reaction-diffusions
items.description: A diffusion equation can be rewritten as a transport equation driven by the score function of the evolving density. Conventional probability-flow formulations, which move particles deterministically with this score-driven velocity, typically conserve total mass.
items.ai_summary: Score-based neural ordinary differential equations develop a Lagrangian method for reaction-diffusion equations by combining characteristic ODEs with a learned velocity field and weighted particle training.

items.title: Node Localization by Multidimensional Scaling with Iterative Majorization
items.description: Node localization aims to estimate the positions of nodes based on collected data from other nodes. Depending on the data characteristics, different procedures are utilized to estimate the locations.
items.ai_summary: Node localization algorithms use multidimensional scaling based on iterative majorization to estimate node positions from diverse data sources and characteristics.

items.title: Typing Matters: Muscle, Language and Typing Behaviour in Live Keystroke Decoding from sEMG
items.description: Surface electromyography (sEMG) from the wrists can recover typed text without a keyboard. It is usually posed as a signal-inference problem: characters are read out of the muscle signal and character error rate is reported offline.
items.ai_summary: A fully causal sEMG typing decoder built on a state space model fuses a traditional decoder with an autoregressive language model to decode live keystrokes from muscle signals.

items.title: Sample-efficient prediction of high-entropy alloy strength through outcome-aware robust sequential learning
items.description: Accurate prediction of high-entropy alloy (HEA) strength can guide composition and processing decisions; however, obtaining tensile-test data for HEAs can be costly and experimentally demanding.
items.ai_summary: Robust Outcome-aware Sequential Experimentation for High-Entropy Alloys proposes a sample-efficient framework for predicting ultimate tensile strength from alloy composition and processing conditions.

items.title: Callo: Serving Cache-Miss Requests with Speculative Decoding on Invalidated KV under Prefill-Decode Disaggregation
items.description: Agent sessions may involve frequent context edits, which effectively invalidate cached KV state and force requests to wait for re-prefill before decoding.
items.ai_summary: Callo is a disaggregated serving system that leverages invalidated key-value states for speculative decoding drafts to reduce agent session latency.

items.title: When to Trust Simulated Patient Responses:Support-Gated World Models for Vasopressor Decision Support
items.description: Clinical world models expose language-model agents to predicted patient responses, but simulations can be unreliable for poorly supported treatments or unfamiliar hospitals.
items.ai_summary: Support-Gated World-Model decision support uses a recurrent dynamics ensemble and a behavior model to predict short-horizon physiological responses while withholding low-support predictions.

items.title: Mesh-Free Weak-Form Regression for Learning Interaction Kernels from Particle Trajectories
items.description: We propose mesh-free weak-form regression for learning interaction kernels from noisy particle trajectories. Our method uses smooth test functions to avoid differentiating noisy data and empirical particle averages to avoid density reconstruction and spatial grids.
items.ai_summary: Mesh-free weak-form regression uses smooth test functions and empirical particle averages to learn interaction kernels from noisy particle trajectories without requiring density reconstruction.

items.title: Dynamic bigraphical Matérn--Whittle processes: learning dependence graphs among spatial-temporal fields
items.description: Many studies record several variables at the same sites over a sequence of periods, such as pollutant concentrations at monitoring stations or case counts of infectious diseases by district.
items.ai_summary: Dynamic bigraphical Matérn-Whittle processes model spatial-temporal fields and their time-varying dependencies across variables using exact posterior estimation over graph eigenmodes.

items.title: Black-Box Uncertainty Quantification for Large Language Models via Ensemble-of-Ensembles
items.description: Reliable use of large language models (LLMs) requires uncertainty estimates that separate ambiguity intrinsic to a prompt from genuine knowledge gaps.
items.ai_summary: A two-level ensemble method uses stochastic decoding and semantic prompt perturbations to decompose large language model uncertainty into aleatoric and epistemic components using black-box sampling.

items.title: PACT: A Decoder-Confidence-Guided Two-Round Receiver for Joint Channel and Phase-Noise Estimation in Sub-THz OFDM
items.description: Frequency-selective fading and oscillator phase noise (PN) jointly impair coded sub-THz OFDM reception.
items.ai_summary: A decoder-confidence-guided two-round receiver combines a complex transformer estimator, equalization, and neural decoding to jointly estimate frequency-domain channels and phase noise in sub-THz OFDM.

items.title: Between Obligations and Evidence: A Participatory Study of Translating the EU AI Act into Technical Requirements
items.description: The EU AI Act imposes technical and organizational requirements for high-risk AI systems, but applying these requirements involves contextual choices about what to measure and what evidence supports a compliance claim.
items.ai_summary: A participatory workshop study investigates how researchers, policymakers, and practitioners interpret EU AI Act obligations and translate them into measurable technical requirements.

items.title: Toward On-Device Markerless 6DoF Tracking of a Physical Manipulative on a Mixed-Reality Headset: A Preliminary Study
items.description: AR-Classroom uses physical models and virtual overlays to help learners explore spatial transformations. To align these overlays on a standalone headset, we developed a markerless six-degree-of-freedom(6DoF) tracker for a LEGO airplane on the Meta Quest 3.
items.ai_summary: An on-device markerless six-degree-of-freedom tracker uses a compact YOLO model and a perspective-n-point solver to align virtual overlays with a physical manipulative on a standalone mixed-reality headset.

items.title: Towards Explainable Sleep Stage Classification using Single-Channel Electroencephalogram
items.description: Automated sleep staging has achieved strong bench- mark accuracy; however, clinical adoption remains limited due to a lack of interpretability.
items.ai_summary: A study evaluating explainable AI methods for single-channel electroencephalogram sleep staging finds that Integrated Gradients consistently achieves the highest mean attribution fidelity across datasets.

items.title: Do Underwater Image Quality Metrics Agree with Human Perception? A Benchmark with Human Choices, Simple Edits and Generative Drift
items.description: Underwater image enhancement is challenging to evaluate due to the lack of clean reference images, so researchers rely on no-reference image quality assessment (NR-IQA) metrics. However, it remains unclear whether these metrics agree with human judgments.
items.ai_summary: TrustUIQA is a benchmark that evaluates 73 underwater image quality metrics against human preferences, revealing that no metric consistently matches human judgments.

items.title: The State Is Not the Bottleneck: A Paged-State Gated-DeltaNet Tile on a Tri-Mode Multicast Mesh, Bit-Exact from RTL to Silicon
items.description: Linear-attention language models replace a growing key-value cache with a recurrent state of fixed size. On an edge FPGA, this state can exceed the on-chip memory and must be paged to external memory.
items.ai_summary: A hardware tile for edge FPGAs computes complete layers of a Gated DeltaNet model while paging recurrent state, demonstrating that weight delivery limits performance rather than state size.

items.title: Graph diffusion transformer for interpretable generation and inverse design of disordered atomic structures
items.description: Atomic disorder offers a potent degree of freedom to tailor material properties, yet the resulting vast configuration space obscures structure-property relations and hinders rational inverse design.
items.ai_summary: Graph Amorphous Diffusion Transformer is a generative model that enables interpretable generation and inverse design of disordered atomic structures while accelerating sampling speed.

items.title: LECAT: Measuring LLM Category Learning from Pretraining Data
items.description: Humans know that airplanes are fast, that this extends to red airplanes, but that it does not hold for broken airplanes. How do LLMs acquire category knowledge that humans learn and apply effortlessly?
items.ai_summary: LeCat is a two-part evaluation and analysis framework that measures how large language models acquire category knowledge and traces how pretraining data influences this learning process.

items.title: CoPre-MoE: Consolidating and Preserving MoE for Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning
items.description: Multimodal continual instruction tuning requires multimodal large language models to sequentially acquire new capabilities without catastrophic forgetting.
items.ai_summary: CoPre-MoE is a shared-and-private mixture-of-experts framework that eliminates parameter redundancy and prevents catastrophic forgetting during multimodal continual instruction tuning.

items.title: LitArc-Bench: Disentangling Text-Specific Reader-Response Dynamics from Position and Lexical Affect
items.description: When model predictions track an unfolding human affect trajectory, alignment may reflect narrative position, affective words, or text-specific reader-response dynamics.
items.ai_summary: LitArc-Bench is a Chinese-language evaluation benchmark that separates text-specific reader-response dynamics from position and lexical affect to measure how well models track human emotional trajectories.

items.title: Fuse-PINN: Combining Finite Element Methods and Physics-Informed Neural Networks to enable massively parallel simulations of non-linear PDEs
items.description: Research in the domain of Physics-Informed Neural Networks applied to PDE modelling has advanced significantly in recent years, providing a wide ecosystem of novel methods.
items.ai_summary: Fuse-PINN is a mathematically robust Finite-Element-Method framework for Neural Networks that enables massively parallel simulations of non-linear PDEs on GPU-based high-performance computing systems.

items.title: Gamer: A Generalist Vision-Language-Action Foundation Model for Long-Horizon Real-Time Game Agent
items.description: Gamer is a generalist agent framework that integrates perception, memory, and multi-step reasoning, trained through continued pre-training, sparse-thinking instruction tuning, and multi-turn reinforcement learning to interact efficiently in 2D and 3D environments.

items.title: Deep Neural Networks Training Efficiency: Does Grokking Modify its Dynamics?
items.description: We study whether grokking, the delayed emergence of out-of-distribution generalization after apparent overfitting, alters training efficiency in deep neural networks, where efficiency is measured as accuracy per unit energy.
items.ai_summary: An analysis of deep neural network training dynamics finds that grokking, or the delayed emergence of generalization, does not materially alter overall training-efficiency dynamics measured by accuracy per unit energy.

items.title: Smart Home Agents Make Capable but Unpredictable Grid Operators
items.description: AI-enabled smart homes are becoming more common across the grid edge. However, there has not been much work on failure response. This area is critical because smart homes operate on the grid edge where failures can cascade down.
items.ai_summary: An outage simulation study evaluates smart home agents acting as grid operators during power outages, identifying new failure categories and limitations in current models.

items.title: Lipschitz-Constrained Discriminators in Generative Modeling: Asymptotic Behavior and Support Mismatch
items.description: We study the asymptotic behavior of optimal discriminators associated to $L-$Lipschitz regularized KL-divergences of two probability distributions $Q$ and $P$ that interpolate between the rescaled Wasserstein$-1$ metric by some parameter $L>0$ and the KL divergence.
items.ai_summary: A study characterizes the asymptotic behavior of optimal discriminators associated with Lipschitz-regularized KL-divergences, motivating improved training strategies for generative models with discrete empirical measures.

items.title: WeatherDreamer: Learning a World Model from Multimodal Earth Observations
items.description: Machine learning weather models now rival operational global forecasts but still start from analyses produced by separate, expensive data assimilation (DA) systems, which for global models are typically updated every six hours.
items.ai_summary: WeatherDreamer is a world model that learns an end-to-end recursive filtering cycle from multiple global observing systems to forecast weather and infer unobserved variables without traditional data assimilation.

items.title: VelServe: Taming Decode Jitters in LLM Inference with Tail-Calibrated Scheduling
items.description: Interactive LLM services must meet latency service-level objectives (SLOs) for the time to first token (TTFT) and the time between tokens (TBT), as streaming and soft real-time applications require predictable token delivery.
items.ai_summary: VelServe is a tail-calibrated scheduler for large language model inference that uses iteration latency measurements to prevent decode jitters and meet latency service-level objectives.

items.title: A systematic comparison of physics-informed neural networks and mechanistic models for epidemic modeling and forecasting
items.description: Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) have recently been applied to epidemic modeling and forecasting with promising results. These methods integrate mechanistic knowledge with data-driven learning.
items.ai_summary: A systematic comparison between physics-informed neural networks and a stochastic mechanistic model shows that physics-informed neural networks achieve better performance on real COVID-19 data while traditional compartmental models remain valuable.

items.title: Where Tree Ensembles Decide: Structural Local Explanation with Decision Predicate Graphs
items.description: Tree ensembles are among the most accurate models for tabular data, yet the computation behind a single prediction is spread over hundreds of decision rules.
items.ai_summary: Local Decision Predicate Graphs gather executed decision rules into a verifiable record to explain tree ensemble predictions by identifying critical feature thresholds.

items.title: Structure makes quantum circuits trainable
items.description: The scalability of variational quantum algorithms is limited by barren plateaus, where gradients vanish exponentially in system size. This worst-case result raises fundamental questions about the trainability of quantum AI models.
items.ai_summary: An analytical framework and sampling algorithm bound the gradient variance of quantum circuits to determine whether a given variational quantum algorithm is trainable before expensive training begins.

items.title: AI-Based Multi-View Echocardiographic Image Synthesis using Dynamic Shape Control
items.description: Although automated methods have improved echocardiographic workflows, progress remains constrained by the need for large, well-annotated datasets.
items.ai_summary: A two-stage AI-based framework combines unpaired GAN-diffusion models and masked video reconstruction to synthesize realistic, temporally consistent multi-view echocardiographic sequences from dynamic heart meshes.

items.title: Vision-Language-Action Models: A Life-Cycle Survey of Design, Training and Deployment
items.description: Vision-language-action (VLA) models adapt web-pretrained vision-language models to output robot actions, so that web knowledge carries over to physical control.
items.ai_summary: A comprehensive survey reviews 88 works on vision-language-action models, categorizing their life cycle across design, training, and deployment for robotic manipulation, navigation, and humanoid control.

items.title: Evaluating Human Sensitivity to Gender Biased AI-Generated Content through Human Assessment of Google's Autocomplete Function
items.description: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly present, but their effects on human users remain underexplored. We tested whether AI-attributed information influences views regarding gender-related statements, a domain where biases are pervasive.
items.ai_summary: An empirical study evaluating Spanish-speaking participants shows that attributing statements to AI does not alter reaction times or agreement judgments regarding gender-related content.

items.title: f-Divergence Self-Play for Tabular Anomaly Detection via Large Language Models
items.description: Anomaly detection in tabular data poses significant challenges due to heterogeneous feature types-mixing numerical, categorical, and textual attributes, which complicate learning meaningful representations of normality.
items.ai_summary: DiSPaT is a self-play fine-tuning framework that uses f-divergence minimization and synthetic pseudo-anomalies to improve large language model performance on tabular anomaly detection.

items.title: DECODE: Decomposable Environments for COntrolled Sequential-Decision Evaluation
items.description: When a sequential decision system falls short of an optimum, its score does not reveal which modifications would improve its decisions. DECODE is a benchmark for testing such modifications through controlled experiments on planning and available information.
items.ai_summary: DECODE is a benchmark comprising partially observed consumer-credit environments that allows controlled experimentation to evaluate the impact of specific modifications on sequential decision solvers.

items.title: Adaptable Watermarking: Transforming Image Watermarking Models via Lightweight Adapters
items.description: We explore the adaptability of neural image watermarking models; the extent to which one watermarking method can be transformed into another through lightweight adaptation.
items.ai_summary: Lightweight adaptation framework that transforms neural image watermarking models into modular architectures, enabling multi-style support without full model retraining.

items.title: Envisioning Agentic Robotics: A New Era of Robotic Systems
items.description: Agentic robotics, centered on an Embodied System 2 formed by a foundation model and embodied harness, requires a shared evaluation framework and research roadmap to achieve reliable physical autonomy.

items.title: Online Switching Control as Learning with Experts
items.description: This paper addresses the problem of online switching control for discrete-time nonlinear systems where a controller is sequentially selected from a finite set of candidates.
items.ai_summary: Adaptive switching algorithm that minimizes cumulative cost in nonlinear systems by reducing online switching control to the experts problem.

items.title: MaskSCD: Bitemporal Mask Classification for Semantic Change Detection in Remote Sensing Images
items.description: Semantic change detection (SCD) identifies where the land surface has changed and which land-cover transition has taken place. Most deep SCD networks predict the change map and the land-cover map of each date with separate per-pixel decoders.
items.ai_summary: MaskSCD is a bitemporal mask classification transformer model that performs semantic change detection in remote sensing images while maintaining consistent change and semantic maps.

items.title: VLAN: Vision-Language Accessible Navigation
items.description: Accessible mobility is user-conditioned rather than scene-intrinsic, as walkable paths for one embodiment are inaccessible to another. Yet, existing benchmarks evaluate traversability under a fixed and limited embodiment.
items.ai_summary: Vision-Language Accessible Navigation is a benchmark containing diverse scenes, trajectories, and embodiment-specific accessibility labels to evaluate physical safety and user-constraint alignment.

items.title: DIRT: Depth-completed Image-based Rendering using Two-band Blending for Live Novel-view Synthesis
items.description: State-of-the-art novel-view synthesis (NVS) methods commonly require per-scene optimization before rendering, limiting their applicability in live settings. Live or ad-hoc NVS, however, demands low-latency rendering during capture and strong generalization to new scenes.
items.ai_summary: DIRT is a non-neural, optimization-free image-based rendering approach that uses depth completion and two-band blending for live novel-view synthesis across heterogeneous sensors.

items.title: Emulating physics-based XCO2 retrievals across OCO-2 viewing modes with compact neural networks
items.description: Operational full-physics retrieval of the column-averaged dry-air mole fraction of carbon dioxide from satellite spectra is computationally demanding. We use singular value decomposition to compress spectra from the Orbiting Carbon Observatory-2 separately by band.
items.ai_summary: Compact multilayer perceptron models that efficiently emulate full-physics carbon dioxide retrievals from satellite spectra across multiple viewing modes and years.

items.title: Marimba: A System One Model for Speech
items.description: Marimba uses frozen Qwen3-ASR features and lightweight readouts to make lexical, turn-end, language, speaker-change, and personal-information decisions from speech, achieving strong detection and calibration on conversational and read-speech benchmarks.
items.ai_summary: Marimba is a speech interface built on frozen audio features to perform typed conversational tasks such as turn detection, speaker counting, and language identification.

items.title: Unlocking Cross-Attention in Label-Scarce Regimes: A Weakly Supervised Approach for Video Semantic Segmentation
items.description: Weakly Supervised Video Semantic Segmentation (WS-VSS) aims to learn temporally consistent semantic object masks in videos using only video-level labels.
items.ai_summary: MemCAM is a transformer framework for weakly supervised video semantic segmentation that stabilizes temporal cross-attention learning through feature-space self-supervision.

items.title: Causal AI-Driven Secure mmWave Beam Alignment with Defensive Variational Autoencoders
items.description: Efficient and secure beam alignment is essential for mmWave communication systems.
items.ai_summary: Causally-aware deep learning framework integrating causal discovery and defensive variational autoencoders to achieve efficient and secure millimeter-wave beam alignment.

items.title: Learning Word-Level Explanations of Text Reuse in Latin Literature with Little Annotation
items.description: Detecting an intertextual reference is only the first step; philologists also need to know how a later author reworked the source.
items.ai_summary: Active learning procedure and pointer network architecture that explain text reuse in Latin literature word by word using minimal manual annotations.

items.title: Experts Across Schemas: Agent-Guided Mixture-of-Relational-Experts for Cross-Database Generalization
items.description: Web platforms record user and item activity in relational databases whose schemas differ from platform to platform, which makes it difficult to transfer predictive models between them.
items.ai_summary: MoREGT is a mixture-of-relational-experts graph transformer combined with an LLM agent that improves cross-database predictive modeling using significantly less pretraining data.

items.title: AI for Parameter Selection in Sample-based Quantum Diagonalization
items.description: Sample-based Quantum Diagonalization (SQD) methods provide a way to compute molecular ground-state energies, but their accuracy and runtime depend sensitively on configuration choices such as the subspace dimension, propagation timestep, and the allocation of a fixed sampling…
items.ai_summary: Machine-learned models predict quantum simulation errors and runtimes from Hamiltonians and candidate configurations to select optimal parameters for sample-based quantum diagonalization.

items.title: When evaluation becomes intervention in clinical AI
items.description: AI judges, models that grade another system's output against a rubric, extend clinical review to the scale at which clinical AI writes. When teams use judge assessments to select a prompt or train a model, the judge becomes part of the intervention.
items.ai_summary: Clinical AI judges that grade other systems can become part of the intervention when used to select prompts or train models.

items.title: PrivacyPR: A Dataset of Real-World Privacy Fixes for Benchmarking Privacy-Aware Code Review
items.description: Coding agents increasingly review code, yet whether they catch the privacy defects that laws such as the GDPR require software to avoid remains largely untested, partly because few datasets connect real privacy defects to their accepted fixes and review context.
items.ai_summary: PrivacyPR is a dataset of real-world privacy fixes and GitHub pull requests that serves as a benchmark for evaluating privacy-aware code review in coding agents.

items.title: Clean Tickets, Wrong Orders: Catching Silent Errors with a Language Model in Your Browser Tab
items.description: A small language model that turns a typed order into structure can fail in two ways. It can print something broken, which any system rejects. Or it can print a clean, well formed order that nobody placed.
items.ai_summary: A fine-tuned language model running entirely within a web browser tab parses and scores typed food orders to detect silent errors without sending text off the device.

items.title: GT-FENG: General Theory of Factual Evaluation and Normative Grounding in Language Models *Author(s)
items.description: Whether a language model's answer is correct often depends on context: the same value can be right under one jurisdiction, date, or legal definition and wrong under another.
items.ai_summary: GT-FENG is a general evaluation framework and open-source Python package that checks language model answers against applicable rules across rule-governed domains like law and policy.

items.title: Right Token, Right Time: From Per-Token Gating to Trajectory-Aware Activation Steering
items.description: Activation steering via sparse autoencoders (SAEs) enables behavioral control of large language models without task-specific fine-tuning.
items.ai_summary: Contrastive Feature Projection and Closed-Loop Adaptive Bernoulli Steering are budgeted gating methods that steer large language model behavior while preserving generation quality.

items.title: From Bytes to Behavior: Request-Level Attribution from Live GPU Hidden States
items.description: Existing memory forensics for machine learning systems typically targets static artifacts, such as model weights or prompt logs, rather than the transient computational states of a live inference process.
items.ai_summary: A non-modifying debugger method acquires per-layer residual-stream activations from a live GPU process to examine the operational behavior of deployed language models.

items.title: TetraCoder: Adaptive Tetrahedral Encoding for Neural Fields
items.description: Implicit and explicit representations of geometry are central in computer graphics applications and come with their pros and cons.
items.ai_summary: TetraCoder is a hash-free adaptive tetrahedral encoding that links an explicit tetrahedral spatial encoder with an implicit signed distance field for 3D reconstruction and editing.

items.title: MamaReason: Unfinished Reasoning and Answer Recovery in Clinical Language Models
items.description: Answer continuation often returns a diagnosis already stated in unfinished clinical reasoning. We study this behavior in MamaReason, adapted from dense Gemma 4 31B, on MamaBench's 217 paired maternal and child-health presentations.
items.ai_summary: MamaReason studies clinical language model behavior where answer continuation returns diagnoses already stated in unfinished clinical reasoning traces.

items.title: Structural Self-Teaching for Compositional Generation in Unified Multimodal Models
items.description: We propose Structural Self-Teaching (SST), a novel framework that enhances compositional image generation in diffusion-based unified multimodal models (UMMs) by leveraging their internal understanding path as a source of structural supervision.
items.ai_summary: Structural Self-Teaching is a framework that enhances compositional image generation in diffusion-based unified multimodal models by converting internal phrase grounding into training-time structural signals.

items.title: NER-D: A cross-domain benchmark for German NER
items.description: We present NER-D, a cross-domain benchmark for German NER comprising 13 datasets spanning 9 domains, including General/Politics, Wikipedia, Legal, Medical, Historical, Financial, Agriculture and Archaeology.
items.ai_summary: NER-D is a cross-domain benchmark for German named entity recognition comprising 13 datasets across 9 domains, used to evaluate proprietary and open-source models under various training settings.

items.title: Deep Bundle Adjustment
items.description: We present \textbf{DeepBA} (\textbf{Deep} \textbf{B}undle \textbf{A}djustment), a graph neural network (GNN) that recovers camera poses, intrinsics, and scene structure from 2D matches across an arbitrary number of views.
items.ai_summary: Deep Bundle Adjustment is a graph neural network that amortizes bundle adjustment to recover camera poses, intrinsics, and scene structure from 2D matches across multiple views.

items.title: Pose-based Neural Clothing for Animated Characters
items.description: Traditional garment simulation for animated characters is a time-consuming bottleneck for artists due to slow simulations and tedious parameter tunings.Recent data-driven methods offer a powerful alternative, capable of learning from a dataset of simulated data to generate…

items.title: ParetoM$^3$: Learning on the Pareto Set under Preference Guidance via Min-Max-Min Optimization
items.description: Learning across multiple inherently conflicting objectives requires selecting desirable trade-offs from the Pareto set.
items.ai_summary: ParetoM3 is a single-loop first-order algorithm that solves a penalty-based min-max-min formulation to compute stationary solutions for preference-guided multi-objective optimization problems.

items.title: Lens: Training-Free Semantic Search for Cross-Tile Object and Scene Retrieval in Satellite Imagery
items.description: We developed Lens, a training-free system for semantic object and scene search across large satellite mosaics that requires no detector trained for the class of interest.
items.ai_summary: Lens is a training-free semantic search system that uses frozen vision transformer features and spatial debiasing to enable real-time cross-tile object and scene retrieval in satellite imagery.

items.title: AcgBoss/manus--ai
items.description: AI Manus is a general-purpose AI Agent system that supports running various tools and operations in a sandbox environment.
items.ai_summary: AcgBoss/manus--ai is a general-purpose autonomous AI agent system that runs code and controls a web browser within a sandbox environment to automate multi-step tasks.

items.title: SandyPandyMandy/manus--ai
items.description: AI Manus is a general-purpose AI Agent system that supports running various tools and operations in a sandbox environment.
items.ai_summary: SandyPandyMandy/manus--ai is a general-purpose autonomous AI agent system that runs code and controls a web browser within a sandbox environment to automate multi-step tasks.

items.title: XTwiNSaraX/ai--manus
items.description: AI Manus is a general-purpose AI Agent system that supports running various tools and operations in a sandbox environment.
items.ai_summary: XTwiNSaraX/ai--manus is a general-purpose autonomous AI agent system that runs code and controls a web browser within a sandbox environment to automate multi-step tasks.

items.title: Dancing Tokens on the Vocabulary Network from LLM Generation
items.description: Large language models (LLMs) generate text one token at a time, yet how a particular generation relates to the geometry learned in pre-training remains unclear. The fundamental explainability of LLMs is elusive.
items.ai_summary: A similarity network built from large language model input embeddings maps generation onto pre-trained geometry to reveal that consecutive generated tokens rarely act as graph neighbors.

items.title: Probabilities of Causation in Nondeterministic Causal Models
items.description: We study probabilities of causation in nondeterministic causal models, where mechanisms may remain intrinsically stochastic even after all latent variables are fixed.
items.ai_summary: Researchers derive sharp analytic bounds on probabilities of causation under various assumptions tailored to nondeterministic causal models using a generic identification program.

items.title: RACE: Ranking-Uncertainty Aware Capacity-Adaptive Customization for Efficient Sequential Recommendation
items.description: Efficient sequential recommendation has emerged as a promising paradigm for providing real-time personalized service.
items.ai_summary: RACE is a framework for efficient sequential recommendation that dynamically adapts model capacity and input sequence length based on a list-wise ranking-uncertainty metric.

items.title: D2ToF: One-Step Diffusion for Depth Super-Resolution from Lightweight Single-Photon LiDAR Waveforms
items.description: Single-photon LiDAR (SPL) sensors offer exceptional temporal resolution and single-photon sensitivity for depth imaging. However, cost-effective SPL arrays typically suffer from extremely low spatial resolutions (e.g. $8\times 8$ pixels), limiting their real-world utility.
items.ai_summary: D2ToF is a one-step diffusion framework that uses distilled diffusion and multimodal guidance to perform depth super-resolution on low-resolution single-photon LiDAR waveforms.

items.title: SCAR: Bridging Coarse Retrieval and Fine Localization through Candidate Reranking
items.description: Natural-language point-cloud localization typically retrieves candidate map cells and then predicts a position inside each candidate, yet the final output is still determined by retrieval order.
items.ai_summary: SCAR is a spatial consistency-aware reranking method that improves natural-language point-cloud localization by selecting the most accurate coordinate hypothesis from a candidate pool.

items.title: Neural Classifiers as Error-Correcting Codes
items.description: A unified framework is proposed that characterizes supervised deep classification as the decoding of error-correcting codes in the Shannon sense.
items.ai_summary: A proposed framework characterizes supervised deep classification as the decoding of error-correcting codes, explaining the geometry of neural representations and improving model quantization and distillation.

items.title: Small Is Not Dead: Distance-Aware Cluster Revival for e-means
items.description: e-means (Bessa et al., 2026) is a recent mini-batch k-means algorithm, now part of the FAISS library, that reaches the error of Lloyd's algorithm about an order of magnitude faster on large embedding datasets.
items.ai_summary: A distance-aware cluster revival method for the e-means algorithm prevents the removal of small, isolated clusters by evaluating inter-centre distances relative to mean squared error.

items.title: NeoResearch: Literature- and Experience-Guided Autonomous Time Series Model Discovery
items.description: Developing effective forecasting models for diverse time-series domains requires substantial expert knowledge, evidence from scientific literature on the web, and iterative experimentation.
items.ai_summary: NeoResearch is an autonomous research framework that uses large language models to mine scientific literature and conduct iterative experiments for discovering lightweight, domain-specific forecasting models.

items.title: Personalization of Basic and Moral Values Guiding LLM-Controlled Assistant Robots
items.description: Personal assistant robots powered by large language models (LLMs) are likely to enter everyday life within the next decade, but the values that should guide their behaviour remain largely unspecified.
items.ai_summary: A study evaluating human value personalization for personal assistant robots finds that contemporary large language models do not automatically adopt desired user values through default behavior or prompt engineering.

items.title: From Pen-and-Paper to Machine-Checked Proofs: Lean for System Identification
items.description: Mathematical proofs in scientific papers are often long and intricate, relying on chains of references to earlier results. This makes it difficult for readers and reviewers to verify each and every step.
items.ai_summary: This paper introduces the Lean 4 proof assistant for system identification and control, demonstrating how to formalize mathematical proofs and check them with software.

items.title: T2ST: Data-Efficient Spatio-Temporal Foundation Models via Temporal Data and Knowledge Transfer
items.description: Spatio-temporal foundation models (STFMs) require large-scale training corpora, yet synchronized observations and spatial metadata are costly to acquire and curate, limiting the availability of suitable data. By contrast, time-series data are abundant and easier to collect.
items.ai_summary: T2ST is a data-efficient training framework that enhances spatio-temporal foundation models by augmenting sparse spatio-temporal observations with auxiliary time series and knowledge transfer.

items.title: MarathonTS: a benchmark of long synthetic time series from window assembly and long-series generators
items.description: Many applications of synthetic time series require a series that is much longer than the windows on which a generative model is trained.
items.ai_summary: MarathonTS is an open benchmark for comparing long synthetic time series generation methods across fidelity, utility, memorization, and computational cost.

items.title: SemRAG: Semantic-Guided Sentence-Level Retrieval-Augmented Sign Language Production
items.description: Sign language production (SLP) aims to generate sign pose sequences that faithfully express spoken-language text while preserving the rhythm and coordination patterns of signing.
items.ai_summary: SemRAG is a semantic-guided retrieval-augmented sign language production framework that retrieves full-sentence signing templates to generate sign pose sequences while suppressing irrelevant motions.

items.title: LaMe: a Joint Latent Mediation Framework for High-Dimensional Systems
items.description: Mediation analysis seeks to understand how an exposure influences an outcome through intermediate variables. However, as increasingly rich datasets become available, hundreds to thousands of potential mediators make these systems difficult to model and hard to interpret.
items.ai_summary: LaMe is a joint linear-Gaussian framework that summarizes high-dimensional exposure-mediator-outcome systems using a small number of latent variables to improve mediation analysis.

items.title: Explanations that Transfer: Interpreting Medical Retrieval with Sparse AutoEncoders
items.description: Medical AI systems that answer users' queries rely on retrieving medical knowledge from large document collections. In this context, finetuning general models on medical datasets can improve retrieval relevance.
items.ai_summary: Method that applies Sparse Autoencoders to medical information retrieval to transform dense text embeddings into semantically interpretable representations that improve retrieval relevance and out-of-domain transferability.

items.title: STaG: Human-Annotation-Free Unsupervised Domain Adaptation for Text-Based Person Retrieval
items.description: Real-world deployment of Text-Based Person Retrieval (TBPR) is bottlenecked by the absence of textual annotations in new domains.
items.ai_summary: Framework named STaG that uses Style-Agnostic Text Alignment and Heterogeneous Graph Memory Alignment to perform human-annotation-free unsupervised domain adaptation for text-based person retrieval.

items.title: ALoMa: Affine Correspondences Beyond Patches
items.description: Affine correspondences (ACs) enable robust and efficient solvers for multiple-view geometry by constraining the local geometry of point correspondences (PCs). Despite their utility in minimal solvers, AC estimation remains understudied.
items.ai_summary: Affine correspondence estimator named ALoMa that uses LoMa keypoint descriptions to jointly learn the full 4-DoF matrix at the image and image-pair levels, improving downstream tasks.

items.title: Who Counts as Exposed? Measurement Choices in an Open, Re-estimable Index of Occupational AI Exposure
items.description: Occupational AI exposure indices are used as inputs to economic analysis, workforce planning, and policy, and the choices built into them decide which workers are described as exposed.
items.ai_summary: Open task-level occupational AI exposure index that varies context and calibration design choices across reasoning models to evaluate their impact on workforce exposure measurements.

items.title: Detection and Classification in Latent Spaces: High-Dimensional Analysis and Validation
items.description: Foundation models produce high-dimensional latent representations in which suitably designed statistical decision rules can be effective yet analytically tractable.
items.ai_summary: Statistical framework for analyzing high-dimensional latent representations of foundation models to predict false-alarm and miss-detection error probabilities for binary and multi-class classification tasks.

items.title: On the Limits of Sufficient Explanations
items.description: We formally characterize the conditions under which sufficient explanations exist for classifiers on structured data such as graphs and strings. We focus on post-hoc explainers that select parts of the input as sufficient explanations.
items.ai_summary: Formal analysis characterizing the conditions under which sufficient explanations exist for classifiers on structured data such as graphs and strings.

items.title: A Multi-Layered AI Pipeline for BPMN Generation from Natural Language
items.description: The automated transformation of unstructured natural language process descriptions into Business Process Model and Notation (BPMN) diagrams remains a challenging task, due to linguistic ambiguity and the difficulty to detect non-adjacent control-flow relationships.
items.ai_summary: Multi-layered pipeline that integrates transformer models, large language models, and ontology population to automatically transform unstructured natural language descriptions into BPMN process diagrams.

items.title: Who Should Be on the Panel? Task-Conditioned Persona Selection for LLM Trading Agents
items.description: Multi-agent LLM systems are built by fixing a cast of roles and then designing how the cast coordinates. Which agents should make up the group for a given task is left to the designer, and the same cast is reused for every task.
items.ai_summary: Multi-agent trading system named FinPanel that uses task-conditioned persona selection to recruit a tailored panel of trader personas for each stock based on a statistical sketch of its trading style.

items.title: Which Model, For Which Variable? Per-Variable Forecast Combination in Sparse ICU Time Series
items.description: Clinical forecasting papers typically report a single best architecture. We show that on multivariate ICU physiology this question conceals variable-specific differences: no architecture is best on every variable, and which model wins changes from variable to variable.
items.ai_summary: Per-variable forecast combination method that combines predictions from multiple models fitted specifically for each variable to improve forecasting accuracy on sparse multivariate ICU time series data.

items.title: Compiling Specialized GPU-Initiated Networking
items.description: Machine learning systems specialize computation to the workload and hardware, but communication remains in generic libraries whose device code and transport decisions are not visible to high-level compilers.
items.ai_summary: Compiler named Obaleth that integrates GPU-initiated communication into intermediate representation to co-optimize it with computation and lower it to specialized transport code for faster distributed machine learning.

items.title: STAMP: Manufacturing-Informed Generative Design and Shape Optimization of Sheet Panels
items.description: Generative design of formed sheet panels must preserve geometric manufacturing conditions while exploring layouts and improving performance. STAMP embeds these conditions directly in the shape representation.
items.ai_summary: Generative design method called STAMP embeds manufacturing conditions directly into shape representations to produce valid sheet metal panels without undercuts or thickness violations.

items.title: DRA-HTR: Disentangling Representation and Adaptation for Handwritten Text Recognition
items.description: Handwritten text recognition (HTR), particularly when applied to historical documents, remains challenging due to the scarcity of annotated data and the substantial domain shifts caused by variations in handwriting styles, document degradation, acquisition conditions, and…
items.ai_summary: Unsupervised generative domain adaptation framework called DRA-HTR adapts handwritten text recognition models to target visual characteristics and integrates language models for post-correction.

items.title: When Copying Is Hard to Beat: A Negative Result in Clinical Assessment Forecasting
items.description: We report a negative result in next-day clinical assessment forecasting: the evaluated models show no consistent advantage over strong persistence-based baselines. Clinicians can view the previous day's questionnaire answers, a plausible source of documentation persistence.
items.ai_summary: Study on clinical assessment forecasting shows that standard models achieve no consistent advantage over simple persistence-based baselines when predicting daily ICU questionnaire items.

items.title: Large Language Model-Empowered Intelligent Agent for Adaptive Fast-Charging Control of Lithium-Ion Batteries
items.description: Fast charging of lithium-ion batteries is a multi-objective control problem that requires reducing charging time and sustaining high energy throughput while suppressing accelerated degradation and safety-critical electrochemical reactions.
items.ai_summary: Large language model-empowered agent called fast-charging control uses reinforcement learning to adaptively manage lithium-ion battery charging while balancing time, degradation, and safety constraints.

items.title: PUMA-Former: Uncertainty-Aware Agentic Computation Offloading in MEO-LEO Satellite Networks With Incomplete Information
items.description: Satellite edge computing distributes mobile workloads across moving processors whose service capacity must be coordinated over time.
items.ai_summary: Uncertainty-aware agentic framework called PUMA-Former manages workload offloading in MEO-LEO satellite networks to improve task completion rates and reduce service delays.

items.title: JFinBench: A Continuously Refreshable Japanese Financial Benchmark from the Latest Certification Exams
items.description: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly applied to finance, creating a need for benchmarks that evaluate their capabilities across financial systems with different regulations and practices.

items.title: PRISM: A Post-Prediction Reliability Framework for Evidence-Guided Correction and Selective Abstention
items.description: A model may produce a prediction with high confidence and still get the outcome wrong. This is a challenge in sequential applications, where the system evolves over time and deployment data may differ from the data used during training.
items.ai_summary: Post-prediction reliability framework called PRISM evaluates model outputs, retrieves historical evidence, and applies corrections or abstains when predictions are unreliable.

items.title: Efficient Poincaré Convolutions through Patch-Statistics Factorization
items.description: Published implementations of the Poincaré convolution in Hyperbolic Neural Networks++ (HNN++) map every overlapping image patch to the Poincaré ball before evaluating its score.
items.ai_summary: Factorized Poincaré convolution layer accelerates hyperbolic neural network training updates by computing patch statistics directly without constructing explicit ball-valued patches.

items.title: Muon Attains $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-3})$ Iteration Complexity under Shuffling
items.description: Muon is a stochastic first-order optimizer for matrix-valued parameters. It maintains an exponential moving average of stochastic gradients in a momentum buffer with coefficient $β$, and orthogonalizes the buffer to obtain the update direction.
items.ai_summary: Stochastic optimizer Muon achieves an O(epsilon^-3) iteration complexity for smooth nonconvex finite-sum problems under shuffling strategies.

items.title: Optimizing Drilling Trajectories in Multi-Material Structures Using Quantum Annealers
items.description: In this work we present a quantum-hybrid optimization approach for planning drilling trajectories on multi-material structures, with the objective of minimizing total energy consumption.
items.ai_summary: Quantum-hybrid optimization approach models drilling trajectories as constrained routing problems to minimize energy consumption and tool-wear penalties in multi-material structures.

items.title: Interpretable weight-space programming builds transparent transformers and brain encoding models
items.description: Neural networks are powerful predictors, yet their opacity limits their usefulness in science, where the goal is explanation rather than mere prediction.
items.ai_summary: Interpretable weight-space programming method uses large language model agents to build transparent transformers and neural encoding models by programming weights in code without backpropagation.

items.title: Folding Language Models into Themselves
items.description: Knowledge distillation usually trains a compact student from scratch, which needs a large amount of data even though the teacher's weights already encode most of what the student has to learn. In this work, we explore building the student directly from the teacher's weights.
items.ai_summary: Concertina is a knowledge distillation method that builds a compact language model directly from a teacher model's weights to recover most of its capabilities efficiently.

items.title: An In-Silico Audit of Topographic Organization in a Multimodal Brain-Response Model
items.description: TRIBE v2 (d'Ascoli et al., 2026) predicts fMRI responses across the cortical surface from video, audio and text.
items.ai_summary: An in-silico audit of the TRIBE v2 multimodal brain-response model reveals that it lacks classic retinotopic and tonotopic organization while retaining strong motion selectivity.

items.title: Contagious Fingerprints: When LLMs Inherit Another Model's Identity
items.description: The fingerprint by which a classifier recognizes the LLM behind a text is usually treated as a fixed property of the model. We show that it is contagious: a model that continues a conversation begun by another model inherits that model's fingerprint.
items.ai_summary: Contagious Fingerprints introduces Lineup, a method that accurately detects model substitution in LLM conversations by generating reference replies on the same dialogue history.

items.title: KnowVis: Dual-View Evaluation and Diagnosis of World-Knowledge Grounding in Text-to-Image Models
items.description: Text-to-image (T2I) models have made substantial progress in visual realism, aesthetic quality, and instruction following. However, real-world prompts often go beyond explicit visual descriptions and require implicit facts, structured knowledge, and domain-specific commonsense.
items.ai_summary: KnowVis is a dual-view evaluation and diagnosis framework that uncovers gaps in world-knowledge grounding for text-to-image models using hierarchical taxonomies and a multimodal judge protocol.

items.title: EcoVGGT: Pinned-Key Inference for Efficient and Streamable Feed-Forward 3D Reconstruction from Long Videos
items.description: Feed-forward multi-view transformers such as VGGT recover the cameras and geometry of a video in one pass, but the cost of their cross-frame attention grows quadratically with the frame count, and their accuracy drops on long videos.
items.ai_summary: EcoVGGT is a training-free inference framework that uses pinned key frames to enable efficient, streamable, and long-video 3D reconstruction with feed-forward multi-view transformers.

items.title: Do Machines Learn Deviance From Their Peers? A Randomized Test of Differential Association With AI Agents
items.description: Differential association theory and its extension, social learning theory, hold that rule-breaking, and the definitions that make it acceptable, are learned through interaction with others. Because people choose their friends, this claim has been hard to test.
items.ai_summary: A randomized experiment using AI agents demonstrates that peer communication significantly influences whether agents adopt deviant or honest behaviors during coding tasks.

items.title: AG-JEPA: Anatomically Guided Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture for Neurodegenerative Representation Learning
items.description: Brain MRI can reveal early signs of Alzheimers disease (AD) before measurable cognitive decline becomes apparent.
items.ai_summary: AG-JEPA is an anatomically guided joint embedding predictive architecture that improves brain MRI representation learning for Alzheimer's disease diagnosis and progression prediction.

items.title: VEPO: Mitigating Multilingual Hallucinations in LVLMs via Visual Evidence-guided Preference Optimization
items.description: Large vision-language models (LVLMs) achieve strong multimodal performance, yet they remain prone to object hallucination---generating answers that are linguistically fluent but visually ungrounded.
items.ai_summary: VEPO is a training-time preference optimization method that reduces object hallucinations in low-resource languages by transferring visual grounding from English using evidence-guided masking.

items.title: Training-point consistency of kernel ridge regression with varying correlation scales
items.description: The scale parameter in kernel ridge regression plays a pivotal role in modeling the correlation structure of data. In modern applications, sampling density and the underlying correlation range often change simultaneously, making a fixed-scale assumption highly restrictive.
items.ai_summary: This paper establishes a unified theoretical framework for the consistency of training-point risk in kernel ridge regression under varying correlation scale parameters.

items.title: Deep Latents, Long Memory: Latent persistence explains temporal correlations in transformer activations
items.description: The hidden layers of Large Language Models (LLMs) are believed to encode representations of the data whose abstraction increases with depth. However, in the absence of an operational notion of abstraction, this statement is hard to test quantitatively.
items.ai_summary: Research demonstrates that deeper layers in large language models encode latent features with longer persistence times, which explains the growth of temporal correlations in their activations.

items.title: Two-Clustering Regime of Token Dynamics in Causal Attention
items.description: We partially resolve Conjecture 1 of [Karagodin et al., Clustering in Causal Attention Masking (NeurIPS 2024)] and extend it to time-dependent parameter regimes.
items.ai_summary: Researchers prove that causal attention dynamics converge to a two-dimensional structure when the largest eigenvalue is positive, enabling the analysis of non-monotone attention dynamics.

items.title: TelePhysica: Agentic Reconstruction of Physically Interactive Scenes
items.description: Direct image-to-video diffusion models entangle pixel synthesis with implicit latent motion, precluding persistent 3D mechanical equilibrium, mid-rollout intervention, and counterfactual force control.
items.ai_summary: TelePhysica is a closed-loop framework that reconstructs an executable physical world from a single photograph to drive stateful 3D interaction and trajectory-grounded video synthesis.

items.title: Learning nonlinear interactions and cross-feature couplings with product-unit residual networks
items.description: Understanding nonlinear feature interactions is crucial in science and engineering, yet standard multilayer perceptrons (MLPs) often capture such interactions only implicitly, leading to entangled representations that can impair robustness and interpretability.
items.ai_summary: Complex-valued product-unit residual networks combine multiplicative product units with residual connections to explicitly model cross-feature couplings and improve prediction performance on scientific benchmarks.

items.title: Agent-as-a-Judge
items.description: Artificial intelligence has progressed from task-specific systems toward general models spanning perception, generation, reasoning, and autonomous interaction, making reliable evaluation essential for comparison, deployment, and post-training feedback.
items.ai_summary: Agent-as-a-Judge is an evaluation framework that integrates multi-agent collaboration, tool use, and planning to actively seek missing evidence and verify factual claims before making judgments.

items.title: Product units in gated recurrent networks enhance prediction of nuclear masses and charge radii
items.description: The prediction of nuclear properties using machine learning can complement theoretical models and advance the exploration of poorly known domains of the nuclear chart.
items.ai_summary: Researchers propose a machine learning technique using gated recurrent units and learnable product-unit mappings to predict nuclear masses and charge radii.

items.title: A$^3$: Adaptive Audio Agent Framework for Collaborative Edge Computing
items.description: Embedded audio agents need a nearby edge server for speed, but a server-dependent agent returns nothing when the link fails.
items.ai_summary: A3 is an adaptive audio agent framework for collaborative edge computing that uses server processing, device-based fallback agents, and a link-aware deadline to ensure reliable response delivery.

items.title: SWAM: Saliency-Weighted Asymmetric Merging for Efficient Vision Transformers
items.description: Vision Transformers (ViTs) achieve strong performance on image recognition tasks, yet their quadratic self-attention complexity over input tokens creates prohibitive computational costs for practical deployment.
items.ai_summary: Saliency-Weighted Asymmetric Merging is a training-based token merging framework that reduces Vision Transformer computational costs while maintaining or exceeding baseline performance.

items.title: coder-smookki/AIst-CyberHack102
items.description: КСТ Визор - AR-помощник обходчика оборудования: шильдик, узлы, дефекты и тип оборудования в реальном времени, датчики, правила и отчёты. Flutter + FastAPI + ONNX, работает в сети цеха без интернета. Хакатон «Кибер 102», команда AIst
items.ai_summary: Coder-smookki/AIst-CyberHack102 is an offline augmented reality assistant built with Flutter, FastAPI, and ONNX to help equipment inspectors identify machinery, read sensors, and record inspections.

items.title: InfiHall-Bench: A Benchmark for Hallucination Evaluation in Autoregressive Text-to-Image Generation
items.description: Hallucination benchmarks for text-to-image generation are predominantly designed around diffusion models, limiting their diagnostic value for visual autoregressive (VAR) models and the development of mitigation methods.
items.ai_summary: InfiHall-Bench is a benchmark of 411 prompts designed to evaluate hallucinations in visual autoregressive models across multiple visual skills.

items.title: FEND: Far-End Detection in Outbound Voice AI Calls
items.description: When a conversational Voice AI agent places an outbound call, the far end may be a live person, a voicemail greeting, an interactive voice response (IVR) system, or increasingly another AI system answering on the callee's behalf.
items.ai_summary: FEND is a detection framework that analyzes audio and streaming transcripts to classify whether an outbound call recipient is a human, voicemail, IVR, or AI system.

items.title: Enrichment-Oriented Virtual Screening of Perovskite Solar Cells through Reinforcement Learning
items.description: Experimental optimization of perovskite solar cells is constrained by combinatorial diversity in absorber compositions, device layers, and processing, which makes virtual screening attractive for prioritizing recipes before fabrication.
items.ai_summary: A surrogate-guided reinforcement-learning framework casts perovskite solar cell recipe generation as virtual screening to enrich candidate shortlists near high-performing experimental neighbors.

items.title: RL$^{\mathrm{RT}}$: On-Device Reinforcement Learning Runtime
items.description: On-device reinforcement learning runs a periodic actor and a learner on one embedded GPU shared with other workloads. Because the learner produces the actor's weights, existing designs stall the actor or let its policy drift.
items.ai_summary: RLRT is an on-device reinforcement learning runtime that uses a tunable refresh bound and a GPU permit to keep policy deadline misses below one percent.

items.title: Multi-level latent-diffusion adaptation for cross-region point cloud segmentation of ancient terraces
items.description: Automated lidar feature detection from lidar point clouds can support archaeological surveys, but models trained in one landscape may transfer poorly to another because of differences in terrain, vegetation, acquisition characteristics, and feature morphology.
items.ai_summary: Multi-level Embedding-space Latent Diffusion trains separate diffusion denoisers on target-domain representations to improve cross-region point cloud segmentation of ancient terraces.

items.title: OnlyTerp/turnpack
items.description: Fewer back-and-forth AI turns. Local MCP context pack + test-gated multi-file ship with automatic rollback.
items.ai_summary: OnlyTerp/turnpack is a local model context protocol server that reduces AI coding agent round trips by combining search contexts, multi-file edits, and test execution into single commands.

items.title: eDIAR: Training-Free Open-Speaker Streaming Diarization for Long Meetings and Large Archives via e-means
items.description: A streaming speaker-diarization method removes the fixed speaker-slot limit by clustering speaker embeddings within slots after all slots are used, allowing unlimited speakers and efficient large-scale linking.

items.title: Aligning AI Teams
items.description: Alignment training on individual LLM agents often fails to transfer to multi-agent teams, but designating a safety lead and having a coordinator publish safety specifications can restore single-agent alignment.

items.title: CANTraj: Recovering Vehicle Trajectories from CAN Signals in Naturalistic Driving
items.description: Open driving releases and usage-based insurance programs often claim to prevent privacy breaches by omitting GPS records when sharing or collecting vehicle data.

items.title: MEM-SQL: Memory-Empowered Text-to-SQL
items.description: A history-aware benchmark and memory-powered method improve Text-to-SQL accuracy and reduce cost by reusing verified SQL components and consulting schemas on demand.

items.title: AI Reviews Are Biased Towards the Appendix
items.description: Large language models used for peer review draw about half or more of their identified weaknesses from paper appendices, whereas human reviewers draw only 8.4% and focus on presentation and core ideas.

items.title: HALO: Human-Aligned Data Collection for WhoLe-body MObile Manipulation
items.description: Learning whole-body mobile manipulation requires demonstrations that coordinate bimanual actions with locomotion across extended workspaces.

items.title: Omodaka9375/browserr
items.description: Servo-based headless browser engine for AI agents. An auditable alternative to embedding Chromium.
items.ai_summary: Omodaka9375/browserr is a Servo-based headless browser engine designed for AI agents as an auditable, fail-closed alternative to embedding Chromium.

items.title: SAOS-3624/see-on-phone
